News.title: Harrowing moment dad who left daughter to die in hot car while he watched porn is found dead by horrified nanny
News.content:
‘HE’S NOT BREATHING’ Harrowing moment dad who left daughter to die in hot car while he watched porn is found dead by horrified nanny

A NEWLY surfaced 911 call has revealed the moment a dad who left his daughter to die in a hot car while he watched porn is found dead by their nanny.

Christopher Scholtes, 38, took his own life in the garage of his £750,000 Arizona home in 2025 – a year after two-year-old Parker’s death.



The little girl died in the back of the family vehicle when Scholtes left her alone on the afternoon of July 9, 2024, as temperatures soared to 42C.

Scholtes took his own life by gassing himself with a car exhaust pipe the day he was set to attend his sentencing.



He faced up to 30 years behind bars.

Chilling never-before-heard audio captured the moment the nanny found his lifeless body.



She is heard saying: “He’s in our home garage. It’s suicide, it’s suicide.

“He’s not breathing, and I can’t find a pulse.”



The carer is then heard telling cops that smoke is coming out of the garage and into the property.

She continues in a panic: “I got them up to get the girls out, but they haven’t, like, gotten the girls out – like everything is kind of chaotic.”

The babysitter adds: “It [the garage] was locked and I had to get the keys to open the garage door and then I found him in there.

“He was supposed to… he had to surrender tomorrow.”

Scholtes, who had a habit of leaving his kids in the car, had pleaded guilty to second-degree murder one month earlier.



Authorities argued Scholtes had left Parker inside the family’s Acura in the driveway of their Marana home near Tucson.

He claimed to have left the toddler in the car at around 12:30pm for 30 minutes with the air conditioning on.

Scholtes claimed he did this as he didn’t want to wake her up from a nap.

Court records later revealed the girl had actually been left alone in the vehicle for over three hours.

He later admitted to knowing the car would automatically turn off its air-con within 30 minutes.



After leaving the car, Scholtes went inside his home to watch porn, play video games and drink beer.

Meanwhile, Parker was left roasting to death inside the car and wasn’t rescued until her mum returned home at around 4pm that day.

Bodycam footage from responding officers showed Scholtes plead with cops and claim he’d only left her outside for “no more than 30, 45 minutes”.

Police told Scholtes at the time: “She’s very hot right now. We’re going to do everything we can.”

Another one of his daughters told police: “My dad started screaming cause he walked outside and he saw that she was in the car still, her lips were purple and she wasn’t breathing.”



After she was found in the car, Parker was rushed to hospital but died within an hour.

A suicide note was left inside the home and Scholtes left a living will on top of the car in case he survived the suicide attempt disabled.

His other children from a previous marriage told cops he would often leave them in the car when they were young.

And Parker’s biological siblings also told police their father regularly left all three of them strapped in the car while he left to run errands.

Scholtes’ own texts with his wife revealed some of his habits.



His partner Erika said in one message after Parker’s death: “I told you to stop leaving them in the car.

“How many times have I told you?”

He responds: “Babe, I’m sorry. Babe, our family. How could I do this? I killed our baby, this can’t be real.”

Medical examiner Daniel Casa claimed Scholtes had begun making suicidal remarks following his daughter’s death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She also catalogued Scholtes’ long list of health conditions, including depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder and ADHD.

News.title: How former lads’ holiday hotspot became a ‘ghost town’ as strict alcohol bans, cop patrols & £3k fines leave bars empty
News.content:
MUSIC is blaring, strobe lights are glaring and the odd drunken boy is spinning on a street corner – but it’s not quite the notorious strip it once was.

A huge revamp has swept across this once-raucous resort and it now seems the classic British “lads’ holiday” no longer fits the luxury image being carefully cultivated by this former party destination.



The nostalgic drive up to Magaluf, in Majorca, didn’t quite give me the same feeling either. Once, leaving the polished luxury of Palma and heading towards the strip felt like an instant shift into chaos.

Now, that jarring contrast has been softened by gleaming five-star hotels and streets that are, at the very least, noticeably cleaner.

There was no sense that this was the place where 18-year-olds who had just broken free from school would come to let loose, away from their loved ones, for the first time.



I’m walking up the strip and it’s almost midnight. I’ve seen more police cars than I have promoters – the first buzzkill for the thrill-seeking tourists who once descended here in their thousands.

The odd promoter does approach me, but with the enthusiasm of someone going through the motions. The old hard-sell tactics and relentless harassment have all but disappeared because there are barely enough revellers to tempt into the bars.

No drunken teenagers are snapping up two-for-one deals, stumbling through the doors giggling, or clutching their friends’ hands as they weave through crowds of 100s to claim their free shot at the bar.

Instead, I was greeted by families and toddlers who had taken their children to the strip for perhaps a glimpse of the lights and a little wander around the empty chairs scattered along the promenade.

This year, authorities in Spain’s Balearic Islands tightened their grip on an alcohol law first introduced in 2020 in parts of Majorca, including Magaluf.



As well as banning drinking on public roads, the rules prevent shops from selling alcohol late at night while imposing tighter controls on party boats.

Any tourists caught breaking the rules could face a fine of up to €3,000.

Palma mayor Jaime Martínez said one of his main objectives is to “correct uncivil attitudes”.



The new clampdown has clearly deterred some tourists, particularly Brits, who bar workers say are no longer flocking to Magaluf in the numbers they once did.

The town has shifted from a budget party strip into a modernised resort zone called Calvià Beach.

Backed by more than €230million in public and private investment, the multi-phase revamp focuses on upscale hotels, upgraded infrastructure and family-friendly cultural spaces.

Emma, 25, a bartender on the strip, told me: “The lack of tourists is definitely affecting business.

“Magaluf has lost all business and its target audience following the revamp.



“British people don’t come at all anymore, it’s only British families and their children.”

Emma, who has been working on the strip for almost a decade, said she used to see all sorts of British boys causing chaos.

She recalled a time when she and her friends had gone to party at one of the bars and ended up in a physical fight with a group of Brit boys.



She described how the Brits, aged between 25 and 35, began throwing chairs at the girls.

Emma said: “Locals have grown tired of the way the tourists act in Majorca.

“It’s like a tourist dumpster and they behave in ways they wouldn’t in their own country.



“That’s why they have tightened the laws but it also means they don’t want to come anymore because they can’t treat it like a dumpster.”

Simon Hood, Executive director of John Mason International, has also issued a warning to Brits jetting off to the party destinations of Majorca and Ibiza in the coming months.

The travel expert said holidaymakers should avoid public drinking and excessive noise at night if they want to avoid penalties, with authorities planning stronger enforcement of key laws throughout the summer.

I found one Brit sitting, sober, in an empty area of the infamous – but now deserted – Piano Bar, while his friends had decided to head further along the strip in search of a bar where there was actually a crowd.

Ben told me: “I came here thinking it would be more wild than this but it’s dead. It’s midnight, where is everyone?”



When I asked him how he felt about the strict alcohol ban, he said: “I don’t even care about that, but clearly others do, that’s why no one’s here,” before laughing.

He added: “My sister came here back in the day, the way she described it is nothing like this.”

Patrolling the top half of the strip, I managed to grab a couple of police officers who had pulled up in their car and were quietly observing the subdued scenes.

One told me: “We have special police just for this area.”

He said that at night there are around six police officers constantly walking up and down the strip.



“It’s to deter criminals,” he told me.

And the clampdown appears to match the figures, with last year being the town’s best tourist season on record in terms of public order.



The number of offences reported to Calvià Police fell 30 per cent across July and August compared with the previous year.

Tiger Tiger was my next nostalgic destination, once booming with tourists and now reminiscent of a movie scene with tumbleweeds drifting across the screen.

Josh, 26, a promoter standing outside the bar, told me: “It’s dying down and it’s not what it used to be. It’s really expensive here now. I’d say prices are pretty similar to Ibiza.

“The police have cracked down a lot on partygoers, and it’s generally deterred rough people.”



Bartender Amine told me as he shook a cocktail: “This summer has felt more strange than ever.”

The 22-year-old added: “There’s absolutely no British tourists anymore. I think it’s because it’s too expensive now.”

The resort’s reinvention shows little sign of slowing.

More than 60 per cent of its hotels are now four and five-star properties, while Calvià council has calculated that the resort managed to halve the decibel levels produced by Magaluf businesses compared with 2024.



Even the town’s attractions have acquired a more polished sheen.

Black metal stands now punctuate the streets as part of a new “selfie route”, directing visitors towards designated vantage points where they can photograph the beach, the sea and tiny Sa Porassa island, or climb into the hills behind the hotels for a panoramic view.

It’s now 1am and the strip has finally begun to stir.

A few more bodies had drifted into the disco-lit streets, but the atmosphere remained a pale echo of the electric frenzy that once made Magaluf infamous.



Earlier, we had eaten beside the newly renovated seafront – another symbol of a resort attempting to redraw its own identity.

For years, Magaluf was regarded as one of Spain’s most notorious holiday destinations, its name practically shorthand for sunburnt excess, cheap booze and badly behaved British tourists.

Its history, however, explains why the transformation has been so dramatic.

During the tourism boom of the 1960s and 70s, Magaluf rapidly blossomed into a major holiday destination. Hotels multiplied, businesses flourished and tourism became a lucrative economic engine for the local community.

But as the years passed, quantity began to eclipse quality.



What had started as a sun-drenched Mediterranean success story gradually mutated into a party capital whose reputation became inseparable from its excesses.

It was routinely mentioned alongside Benidorm and Lloret de Mar as a byword for unruly mass tourism, while the resort repeatedly made headlines over balconing deaths, brawls and alcohol-fuelled excess.

But that version of Magaluf increasingly feels like a relic.

Today’s Calvià Beach – the new brand name adopted by hotel chain Meliá International – is cleaner, quieter and considerably more manicured, and it seems Brit teens don’t want any part of it.

News.title: Ex-soldier ‘murdered gran, 75, and battered her husband with metal pole after bursting into their home during burglary’
News.content:
OAP TRAGEDY Ex-soldier ‘murdered gran, 75, and battered her husband with metal pole after bursting into their home during burglary’

A FORMER soldier allegedly murdered a great-grandmother and battered her husband with a metal pole during a burglary, a court heard.

Rose Smith, 75, and Ronald Smith, 81, were watching TV in Finsbury Park, North London, when four men burst in and made demands for cash, it is said.

The gran was found collapsed in a hallway at around 9.20pm on August 11 after a neighbour flagged down police.

Rose was rushed to hospital but tragically could not be saved and was declared dead the following day.





A post-mortem examination gave the preliminary cause of death as a stroke, which the prosecution alleges was caused by the incident.

Jeffrey Dean Rose, 46, appeared at Barkingside Magistrates’ Court today charged with manslaughter, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and aggravated burglary with intent.

The court was told a man armed with a metal police attacked Ronald, who “had to raise his arms to protect his face”.

Prosecutor Grace Bussey said: “They were told to sit on the sofa and their phones were taken off them.



“When Mrs Smith left the living room she collapsed in the hallway.”

Suzanne John, defending, said dad-of-two Jeffrey Rose was a private investigator from 2012 to 2016.

She told the court he then became a soldier but was discharged due to the Covid pandemic and instead became a bin man.

The defendant was remanded in custody to appear at the Old Bailey on September 22.



In a statement, Rose’s family said: “This is the most devastating loss our family could ever have imagined.

“Rose was a truly wonderful, outgoing woman who was loved by so many people.

“She loved bingo, going to cafes with her friends and, above all, spending time with her family.

“She treasured the time she spent with her children, grandchildren and great-grandchild.

“She was the life and soul of every party. She had a wonderful personality, a big heart and a way of bringing laughter and happiness wherever she went.



“We want people to remember Rose for the person she truly was — loving, fun, kind, sociable and full of life.”

News.title: Madeleine McCann suspect Christian Brueckner to face retrial over rape in ‘game changer’ for missing toddler case
News.content:
OFFICIALS are set to send Christian Brueckner back to court over rape claims and reignite the Madeleine McCann case against him.

Germany’s top prosecutor has secured a hearing to tell an appeal judge Brueckner, 50, should not have been cleared of rape in 2024 – and must face a retrial.



Crucial evidence with the power to put Brueckner behind bars for good was revealed to have been left out of the trial by The Sun – and could now finally be used against him.

The hearing announcement, set for January, has been hailed by Maddie investigators in Europe as “a game changer” as they realise a retrial will almost certainly follow under the German system.



A second trial is seen as crucial for the McCann case as it could put fiend Brueckner in jail for good. That is when investigators have said they would finally charge the sex offender over Maddie.

A source close to the case in Germany said: “This is a case with very little good news – and no prospect of a happy outcome.



Watch The Sun’s documentary: Madeleine McCann: The Evidence on Prime Suspect Christian Brueckner

“But for those who want to see Brueckner charged over Madeleine, this new court date is a gamechanger.

“The way the German system works means every part of the original trial will be considered – and the judge overseeing it is incredibly sharp. She will miss nothing.

“Maddie investigators realise for the first time, there is a genuine will to see a retrial and for something to be done about Brueckner.”



Drug dealer Brueckner was cleared of the rape of Irish holiday rep Hazel Behan in 2024 allowing him to sensationally be freed last year.

He has now been ordered to appear before a court in Leipzig at the start of next year in front of one of Germany’s leading appeal judges, Judge Loisa Bartel.

A decision on the appeal would follow in as little as a few days. It means Brueckner could face a second rape trial as soon as next spring – although he would not be held on remand.



A letter from the court to expected attendees reads: “Criminal proceedings against Christian Stefan Brueckner for aggravated rape, among other offences.

“In the above-mentioned criminal proceedings, the scheduling of the main hearing of the appeal on points of law (Revision) concerning the appeals lodged by the Public Prosecutor’s Office and the private accessory prosecutors (Nebenklägerinnen) is now pending.

“The main appeal hearing is therefore to take place in front of the Federal Administrative Court in Leipzig on Monday, 11 January 2027.”

Prosecutors in Germany still believe he kidnapped and killed Madeleine, three, in 2007 – while British cops have also stepped up their enquiries into the paedophile and are looking at the possibility of extraditing him to the UK.

Their tactic has been to secure a second rape conviction against the sicko that would allow a court to cage him for life – and embolden German cops to prosecute him over the McCann case.



As long as Brueckner remains free cops remain panicked he could flee Germany and go into hiding – a tactic he has used in the past when facing suspicion over crimes.

Rolling 24-hour police surveillance of Brueckner was scrapped earlier this year raising fears tracking the sex offender could finally slip out of the country.

But this has now been reinstated, however, as German officials realise it is essential for preserving the suspect’s safety in the wake of low-level vigilante attacks.



Brueckner has been laying low since publicly declaring he “f***ing hates Maddie” in a vile video outburst published on YouTube.

Three-year-old Madeleine, of Rothley, Leics., vanished from the Ocean Club, in Praia da Luz, Portugal on May 3 2007 while on holiday with her family.

Brueckner was named as the prime suspect in the disappearance and murder of the tot in 2020 by German cops.

Police have been able to confirm his phone was near Ocean Club, where the McCanns were staying, around the time Madeleine disappeared on May 3, 2007.

Witness Helge Busching claims a year later Brueckner all-but-confessed to him at a music festival, in Spain, saying “she didn’t scream” as the pair discussed the McCann case.



Investigators say they have physical evidence Madeleine is dead but no forensic proof tying Brueckner to the case.

An exclusive Sun investigation – aired as a Channel 4 documentary in May – revealed cops are in possession of images that help contribute to their understanding Maddie is dead.

They also have appalling child abduction stories where Brueckner daydreams about snatching and abusing young girls – including one outside a kindergarten.

He even brags about his desperation to “take something small and use it for days” in online chats with another paedophile.

Despite the overwhelming circumstantial evidence, investigators have been reluctant to chargeover the casess, fearing the lack of forensic evidence would harm their chances.



They were also spooked by a court clearing Brueckner of rape and a string of sex assaults last year – the acquittal which put him on the path to freedom.

Since Brueckner’s release, the Met have significantly stepped up their activity on the case, including jetting to Portugal last year to re-interview witnesses, as revealed by The Sun.

Last week we told how UK cops had taken possession of bombshell files on Brueckner from Germany.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brueckner has refused to answer police questions over the case but has insisted he is innocent in letters. His lawyers continue to protest his innocence on all matters.

He was released from prison on September 17 when his seven-year sentence for the 2005 rape of a woman, 72, in Praia expired, with German cops insisting their Maddie investigation would continue.

News.title: When does summer end? Date autumn 2026 will officially start and the Met Office long-range weather forecast
News.content:
WITH August drawing to a close, millions of Brits are asking whether it is time to pack away the suncream or if summer still has one last trick up its sleeve.

The official answer depends on whether you ask a meteorologist or an astronomer.



Meteorologists have a fixed date on the calendar, while astronomers follow the movement of the Earth and stars.

When does summer officially end?

Summer‘s end – and autumn’s beginning – can have two start dates depending on whether you follow climate records or the night sky.



There is no single “correct” answer as to which system you want to use to define the end of the season.

Meteorological summer always starts on June 1 and finishes on August 31 – with meteorological autumn kicking off the very next day.

Astronomical summer ends at the Autumnal Equinox – which in 2026 lands on September 23.

What is Meteorological Summer?

Meteorologists split the year into four equal seasons made up of three full calendar months each.

Summer spans June, July, and August, drawing to a close on August 31.

Autumn takes over for September to November, and winter closes out the year through December, January, and February, before spring covers March to May.



By fixing these dates to months, weather forecasters and climate scientists can easily compare rainfall, temperature stats, and weather patterns.

What is Astronomical Summer?

Astronomical autumn is governed by the Earth’s orbit around the Sun.

Astronomical Summer officially concludes at the exact moment of the Autumnal Equinox, when the Sun aligns directly above Earth’s equator.

Daylight hours in the Northern Hemisphere actually begin shrinking right after the Summer Solstice in June.

But as Earth moves along its orbit, its fixed axial tilt causes the Northern Hemisphere to receive progressively less direct sunlight, steadily shortening the days until day and night reach near-equal length at the equinox.



Once this tipping point passes, nights become longer than days, causing temperatures to drop more rapidly as daylight hours continue to diminish.

Because Earth takes roughly 365.25 days to complete its orbit, the exact calendar date of summer’s end shifts slightly every year.

It almost always lands between September 21 and 24, and in 2026, will fall on Wednesday, September 23.

When do the clocks change?

The end of summer also brings the end of British Summer Time (BST).

The clocks go back one hour on the last Sunday of October – in 2026, that’s Sunday, October 25 – returning the UK to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).



While we lose an hour of evening daylight, the trade-off is an extra hour of sleep on Sunday morning and slightly brighter starts to the day.

What is the Met Office’s long-range forecast?

While meteorological autumn is around the corner, will it actually feel like the seasons are changing?

The Met Office’s long-range forecast predicts a mix of downpours, thunder, and late heat spikes across the UK.

The shift from August into September will bring unsettled conditions across much of the country.

According to the Met Office, “an unsettled period is likely, with showers or longer spells of rain possible across many parts of the UK.”



Heavy downpours are expected to break out widely, with the weather agency warning that “some heavy rain is likely, perhaps with some thunderstorms too.”

Forecasters add that “rainfall amounts will probably be above average for the time of year and there is potential for some strong winds at times.”

But despite the wet outlook, summer isn’t surrendering completely.

The Met Office highlights that “some drier and more settled interludes could develop at times,” though these will likely be short-lived.

Temperatures will remain near average overall, but “some short-lived warm or very warm spells are possible, especially in the south.”



Heading further into September, changeable weather will continue before potentially settling into a drier, warmer spell.

Forecasters expect a “continuation of the generally unsettled conditions at first with showers or longer spells of rain across many areas, perhaps heavy and thundery in places.”

But a welcome turnaround could arrive later in the month.

The Met Office says: “Further into September, drier weather may become more prevalent, especially in the south and southeast, with any more unsettled conditions tending to become more likely further north and northwest.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Temperatures are also tipped to climb as autumn approaches.



While conditions will stay “near normal at first,” forecasters note temperatures “may become warmer later, with the possibility of some hot spells in the south.”

News.title: Newborn baby girl found dumped in rubbish bag with umbilical cord still attached after woman thought she heard cat cry
News.content:
A NEWBORN baby has been found inside a rubbish bag by an innocent local who thought she heard a crying cat.

The little girl was discovered with her umbilical cord still attached dumped inside a plastic sack covered by a black towel in Brazil on Monday.



She was found after a resident on Otavio Ignacio da Silva Street, Parana, thought she heard one of her cats wailing and went outside to check.

The bystander, named Katia Andreja Bege, then checked the neighbouring yard before making the grim discovery.



Katia found a transparent plastic bag covered with a black cloth.

To her horror, there was a newborn girl with her umbilical cord still attached inside.

Astonishing footage showed Katia holding the tiny newborn in her arms after she had been discovered.

She appeared to cradle her while thanking God for finding her.

Katia said: “Thank God I found her!”

In the clip, a neighbour who filmed the baby shortly after the discovery can also be heard describing what had happened.



The neighbour said: “Goodness, look what my neighbour found inside the rubbish bag thrown there in the yard.

“She still has the umbilical cord! My God! She has just found her!

“She thought it was her cat crying, went to look and saw a child inside the rubbish. My God!”



Paramedics rushed to the property and took the baby to the Hospital de Clinicas in Curitiba, where she arrived at around 4am.

Doctors said the baby had been born at full term after 40 weeks of pregnancy and weighed 2.8kg.

She arrived with severe hypothermia but was breathing spontaneously.

The newborn examination in the neonatal intensive care unit where medics found she had suffered two fractures, involving her collarbone and thigh bone, at birth.

Her birth did not take place inside a hospital, they said.



Despite arriving with severe hypothermia and injuries, the newborn’s condition was described as stable.

Initial police investigations indicated that the baby’s mum was a pregnant teenager who had given birth that morning before leaving the newborn in the empty lot opposite her home.

Police chief Joao Paulo Pelaez claimed the teenager believed the baby was dead and then chose to leave it at the site.

The teenager told police she had hidden the pregnancy because it had resulted from rape, reports say.

She and her parents were taken to the police station to give statements.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The teenager will face trial while remaining free.

The Parana Civil Police have opened an investigation into suspected abandonment of a vulnerable person.

News.title: Map reveals 58 locations hit by 19-hour thunderstorm warning tomorrow – as hail and heavy rain to batter parts of UK
News.content:
DOZENS of locations are set to be battered with torrential rain and thunderstorms tomorrow and Thursday after prolonged periods of drought.

The impacted areas may experience public transport delays and cancellations, as well as potential road closures and flooding.

The Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for heavy rain and thunderstorms in 58 locations on Wednesday and 56 locations on Thursday.



Heavy downpours are forecast across a number of major cities, including Greater London, Manchester and Birmingham.



Weather warnings officially come into force from 3am tomorrow morning, with rainfall focussed on the East and North West of England and the Midlands, with yellow alerts continuing until 10pm.

The Met Office has warned of a small risk of flooding and disruptions from thunderstorms tomorrow, but some of the worst hit areas could be hit by 1.5 to 1.9 inches of rain in just two to three hours.

Moving into Thursday, another yellow weather alert comes into effect, with thunderstorms and heavy rain said to lead to some disruptions.

Thunderstorms could begin from 6am on Thursday, with the downpours hitting the West of England and larger parts of Wales, with conditions expected to settle by 10pm.

During Thursday’s thunderstorms, the Met Office says there is a small chance that homes and businesses could flood quickly.



The forecaster has further warned that there is a “small chance of fast flowing or deep floodwater causing danger to life”.

This inclement weather comes as nearly three-quarters of England and the entirety of Wales face drought as a result of prolonged dry conditions, with 45million Brits affected.

As water levels dwindle, nine water companies have introduced hosepipe bans for at least 27 million customers across England and Wales.

News.title: Victim stabbed to death in broad daylight horror attack at council HQ near Wembley – as emergency crews swarm scene
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE ATTACK Victim stabbed to death in broad daylight horror attack at council HQ near Wembley – as emergency crews swarm scene

A PERSON has tragically died after a horror broad daylight stabbing at a council HQ near Wembley Stadium.

Officers cordoned off the Brent Civic Centre in Wembley, North West London, after the horror unfolded this afternoon.



Metropolitan Police and London Ambulance Service (LAS) crews rushed to the HQ at around 2.25pm.

Staff and visitors in the building, which is home to Brent Council, were also reportedly evacuated as the horror unfolded.



One person was treated at the scene but was tragically pronounced dead, despite the best efforts of emergency medics.

Eyewitnesses reported seeing someone “on the floor” on the balcony in the library after the attack.

One wrote on social media: “I was in the library on the mezzanine level when it happened.

“From what I could see from the balcony was somebody on the floor and splatters of blood. I have no more information than that.”



Another wrote: “I was at the exact same place where the stabbing happened and had gone up to the first floor about ten minutes earlier.

“A staff member walked into the meeting room and told us to evacuate because someone had been stabbed.

“What I witnessed on the way down was unreal.”

Air ambulance crews were among the emergency response scrambled following reports of the stabbing, according to the LAS.



Incident response officers and paramedics in fast response cars were also dispatched to the chaotic scene.

Images taken from outside the building show several police officers gathered around the entrance.

A number of emergency vehicles, including ambulances and police cars, were also seen parked outside the council HQ.

A spokesperson for the service said: “We were called at 2:25pm to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre, Wembley, HA9.



“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer.

“We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

More than 2,000 employees work in the building – including local councillors.

The Sun has contacted the Metropolitan Police for comment.

News.title: Barcelona fire LIVE: 'Explosion' heard as blaze burns 25 hectares and residents told 'stay indoors'
News.content:
An image of the blaze taken from a Ryanair plane

A huge fire has broken out in Barcelona, with smoke visible from a Ryanair flight amid unconfirmed reports of an explosion

A large fire is burning in Barcelona, with around 25 hectares of land affected and residents in two neighbourhoods told to stay indoors.

Mobile phone alerts have been sent to people in Torre Baró and Ciutat Meridiana, warning them to close their doors and windows and not go outside due to the vegetation fire.

People posting on X have reported hearing an explosion, while a high-voltage tower in the area is believed to have been damaged. The explosion report has not yet been confirmed by authorities.

Spain’s 112 emergency service has received 1,074 calls about the blaze, while firefighters continue to tackle the flames.

The emergency warning tells residents: “Close doors and windows and do not go out on the street. In case of emergency, call 112.”

News.title: Should Brits get their licences taken away for dangerous driving videos? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should Brits get their licences taken away for dangerous driving videos? Take our poll and have your say

As a ghoulish social media trend sees young motorists risk everything on the road for likes, but should those who upload dangerous driving videos face serious penalties?

View 2 Images Liberty Mitchell, 21, filmed herself speeding and swerving in a Mini Cooper for Snapcha (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

Campaigners are calling for those who upload dangerous driving videos to be stripped of their licences, to prevent further bloodshed.

‌



While those who are found guilty of a drink-driving offence automatically lose their licence, no such legislation is in place to tackle an alarming online trend. As seen by the Mirror, young people are turning to social media platforms such as TikTok to share content of themselves, risking their lives on the road in the name of likes.

‌



Some of these clips show youngsters going 'ghost mode', speeding along narrow, winding country lanes with their lights off. Others partake in wrong way motorway driving stunts. This is a deadly trend that cannot be normalised and, as seen in recent weeks, the effects of reckless driving, whether filmed or not, can be catastrophic.

‌



In the early hours of Saturday, August 22, two police officers, PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died following a nightmare collision near Middlesbrough, Teesside.

A Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 dual carriageway collided head-on with the police vehicle that had been assisting in a search for the car. All five occupants of the Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18 - died instantly.

‌



It quickly emerged that a TikTok profile believed to belong to Saddington frequently featured footage which glorified dangerous driving. One video, deleted shortly after the crash along with the account, appeared to show Saddington in a high-speed police chase alongside four other youngsters.

View 2 Images PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were both killed in the horror wrong-way smash (Image: Getty Images)

This tragedy came mere days after another wrong-way motorway crash in County Kildare, Ireland. Five teenagers - Jeremy O'Brien, 18, Alex McCarthy, 17, Joey Carthy, 15, Jack Kennedy, 17, and Kamil Pustkowski, 17 - died when their BMW, travelling the wrong way down the M9 motorway at more than 74mph, crashed head-on into a Hyundai.

‌



The Hyundai had been carrying three sisters, Ella, Niamh, and Alma Kinsella, in their 20s and 30s, and a seven-year-old boy, all of whom were driving to Dublin Airport for a family wedding. The five teenagers were killed at the scene, while the three sisters sustained severe injuries. The young boy suffered a broken leg.

It's an issue that has sparked concern for some time. In December 2022, newly qualified driver Liberty Mitchell recorded Snapchat videos of herself speeding at almost 100mph in a 60mph zone.

Overtaking three vehicles on the wrong side of the road near Aldsworth, Gloucestershire, the then-18-year-old lost control of her Mini Cooper and caused a multi-car pile-up, killing taxi driver Octavian Codreanu and his passenger, teacher Moyra Whelan.

Article continues below

This week, the Government has demanded that social media companies remove any content which shows people driving dangerously. Speaking with reporters during a visit to Kyiv on Monday (August 24), Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated: “Anybody who glorifies dangerous driving is doing something that’s truly reprehensible.”

News.title: SUV drivers in UK city to pay new tax as council introduces England first payments
News.content:
SUV drivers in UK city to pay new tax as council introduces England first payments

Angry motorists in Bath are hitting back at the council's plans to introduce new charges based on the size of their vehicles, which come on top of existing emissions charges

View 5 Images Many motorists have been left furious by the move (Image: Getty Images)

SUV owners driving in one of the UK's most picturesque cities will soon have to fork out cash for a specialised tax introduced by a local council.

‌



In an England first, Bath has become the first city in the home nation to introduce an "SUV tax", which will charge drivers more to park bigger cars at home. The decision was taken by Bath and North East Somerset Council, which plans to introduce size-based pricing for residents' parking permits.

‌



But angry motorists have hit back at the plans, which came following a public consultation in 2025, stating the council is doing things that "don't make sense".

‌



View 5 Images Bath residents already pay emissions charges (Image: Getty Images)

The authority revealed it would be pushing ahead with the plans following its consultation last week, despite the angry backlash, ushering in a first for England. A similar policy was pursued in Wales last year, with another scheme dubbed an "SUV tax" introduced in Cardiff.

The Bath version of the scheme would see supplementary charges introduced for larger vehicles, while smaller vehicles are handed discounts.

‌



The policy was launched on August 25, and would in action see owners of smaller Smart cars get a £20 permit discount every year. Drivers who opt for much larger cars, however, including the Land Rover Discovery or Ford Galaxy, would pay up to £41 more. The highest premiums would be reserved for Ford Transit owners who sprung for the manufacturers' largest option.

View 5 Images Car owners could be asked to fork over more than £100 extra for the largest cars (Image: Getty Images)

They would have to pay a maximum of £112, a price Bath's council says will help encourage large car owners to spring for smaller, safer models.

‌



The charges for car size would be applied on top of emissions-based payments motorists are already asked to make based on how polluting their cars are. The size-based charges are planned to operate on a similar system, and, where no data is available, be based on people's self-submitted photo evidence.

The council also says it will increase the cost of a residents' parking permit by 20% generally and begin phased increases to the cost of visitor permits.

View 5 Images The council also plans to increase residents' parking permit costs by 20 percent (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Defending the decision, council cabinet member Joel Hirst said: "Research shows that larger vehicles like SUVs pose a greater risk to pedestrians and cyclists in collisions, with children particularly vulnerable.

"By introducing size-based permit charges, we are encouraging the use of smaller, safer and cleaner vehicles." Bath residents have slammed the plans as "outrageous" and claimed they will unfairly target families and people with disabilities, who need the larger vehicles for their additional needs.

Bob, 63, a retired Bath taxi driver, said he might not mind the policy if Bath's council was actively improving the city's public transport service. He said: "I was driving in this town for 20 years, and at the time, I had to pay something like £80 to £100 for residential parking."

‌



View 5 Images Some residents have said they believed the pricing plan was a 'good idea' (Image: Getty Images)

"If that weren't bad enough, they then add injury to insult by saying, 'now we're going to charge you by the size of your car as well. The things they are doing don't make sense. I wouldn't mind so much, but they're not improving the public transport system. I don't think it's going to improve the congestion in the city, because it doesn't matter how much they put the charges up - people will still pay the charges.

"People will still come into the centre of town because they have to, to function." Despite the concern, some residents were in favour of the changes, including 63-year-old Jayne Mallon, who said previously: "I think it's a good idea. Bigger vehicles should pay more - they take up more space and give out more pollution."

Article continues below

Similar charges were introduced last autumn in Cardiff, which became the first local authority in the UK to introduce a parking premium for larger vehicles. They said the plans were "to encourage drivers to switch to smaller vehicles," amid a backlash against large SUVs.

The council said it carried out initial public consultation on the proposals in Bath last year. It said feedback showed that 50 per cent of respondents supported introducing size-based charges or discounts for residents' parking permits.

News.title: Richard Osman tips Prince Harry to star on huge TV show that he would be 'great' on
News.content:
Richard Osman tips Prince Harry to star on huge TV show that he would be 'great' on

Richard Osman has tipped Prince Harry for a career on a BBC TV show after praising his "very good" appearance on a popular podcast during his visit to the UK last month

View 3 Images Harry and Meghan shocked the world when they announced their plans (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Television presenter and producer Richard Osman has tipped Prince Harry for a broadcasting career after praising what he described as a "very good" showing on a podcast during the Prince's visit to the UK in July. Harry appeared on the Joe Marler Will See You Now podcast, and Richard believes the appearance could signal a future in front of the camera for King Charles's youngest son.

‌



Speaking on The Rest Is Entertainment, he said: "I saw him on the Joe Marler podcast. He's very good on things like that. And I think you could build a fairly nice media career for Harry where he just appears on television every now and again. If I was his advisor, and I can exclusively reveal that I'm not, I'd have him meeting people."

‌



Richard then floated a particular proposal for Harry, suggesting he would be ideally suited for a spot on Michael McIntyre's The Wheel. The game show, fronted by comedian McIntyre, features seven celebrities positioned around a wheel, each bringing their own specialist knowledge. It broadcasts on BBC on Saturday evenings, reports the Express.

‌



Richard said: "I'd put him on The Wheel tomorrow, with Michael McIntyre. He'd be great on The Wheel. Michael would look after him, he'd look good if he got something right, he'd look self-depreciating if he got something wrong. I wouldn't put him on The Traitors or I'm A Celebrity or something like that."

Harry and Meghan have denied holding a secret meeting with Christian and Geri Horner as they look to reintegrate back into UK life. It remains to be seen what Harry does for work on his return, but his schedule for several charity commitments in Britain in September were already confirmed.

View 3 Images Richard Osman offered Harry some career advice (Image: Getty Images for BAFTA)

‌



He will attend the WellChild Awards in London as he maintains his backing for the event, which honours the bravery of seriously ill children.

The Invictus Games will also take place in the UK next summer, with Birmingham selected as the host city. It is understood the family will establish a base in the Cotswolds where they are thought to have friends.

Richard Osman, though, seemingly had his own plans for Harry. Getting into his stride, Richard he pitched his own concept for Harry - a fresh programme titled Harry's Special Forces, which he described as a hybrid of DIY SOS and the beloved 1990s game show Challenge Anneka.

‌



Elaborating on the idea, he said: "I've got a show called Harry's Special Forces. It's like DIY SOS meets Challenge Anneka. It is exactly that thing of a house needs rebuilding, a community centre needs rebuilding.

View 3 Images Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are returning to the UK (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS.com)

"But he does it with a bunch of army veterans, people who have been injured in the line of conflict. And they build something and put something together.

Article continues below

"At the same time he's showing these veterans, they're putting their skills out there for employers, it's feel-good."

The comments come as Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are anticipated back in the UK before August draws to a close following a remarkable Megxit reversal. The former working royals have registered their children at school and are understood to be preparing for a stay in Britain "for an extended period of time".

Speculation has been rife about what the couple will pursue professionally. Meghan has been earmarked for a potential return to acting, with a part in Guy Ritchie's Netflix series The Gentlemen reportedly on the cards.

News.title: Mum of teen killed in wrong-way M9 crash apologises to family left in hospital
News.content:
Mum of teen killed in wrong-way M9 crash apologises to family left in hospital

Mourners today gathered for the funeral of Jack Kennedy, 17, who died alongside four others after the car they were travelling in was driven the wrong way down the M9 motorway in Ireland

Jack Kennedy: Funeral held for teenager killed in M9 crash in Ireland

The mother of one of the five young people killed when their car went the wrong way down the M9 in Ireland, before crashing into another car, has apologised to a family left in hospital.

‌



The funeral mass for 17-year-old Jack Kennedy, who died in the crash on the M9 in Co Kildare last weekend, also heard calls to “please, please, please, stop” engaging in criminal activity.

‌



Sisters Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella, who are aged in their 20s and 30s, were rushed to hospital after their car was struck by the vehicle travelling the wrong way. They were travelling with a child, who was also hospitalised, when their Hyundai was hit by the BMW at around 3am on August 16.

‌



Garda officers were stationed in Kildare ahead of Jack's funeral today, but less than was seen at the services held last week for the other four who died in the crash.

View 4 Images Jack Kennedy

Police probe as several motorists seen driving wrong way on M6 following crash READ MORE :

Jack died alongside Jeremy O’Brien, Kamil Pustkowski, Joe Carthy and Alex McCarthy when their car collided head-on with the other vehicle.

‌



Jack’s mother Sarah spoke at the funeral at St Michael’s, Athy, Kildare, on Tuesday morning. She apologised to the family still recovering in hospital as a result of the crash.

“Five young boys made a bad choice,” she said. “Five young boys paid the ultimate price. Five families lost their babies. Five families got a life sentence. May they all rest in peace.

View 4 Images The cortege for Jack Kennedy makes its way through Athy, Co Kildare, ahead of his funeral at St. Michael's Parish Church (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

‌



“Secondly, we all want to send our deepest, heartfelt apologies to the families who were injured. You are all in our thoughts and our prayers. We pray to God that you all make a full recovery and once again, we are sorry.”

In the eulogy, Canon Frank McEvoy referred to anger that has been expressed on social media surrounding the incident. He said: “Words can hurt, and words have the power to heal. It’s also true of actions. Our actions can hurt people, and our actions can heal people.

“In all those situations, we’re responsible for the words that we use, and above all, we’re responsible for the actions that we take.”

‌



He said the feeling in the parish after the crash was “one of shock, confusion, disbelief, and above all, anger”. “Anger is a very dangerous emotion, and when it starts to curdle and get going in the community, anything can happen,” he said.

View 4 Images Ella Hendricken (L), Niamh Kinsella (C) and Alma Kinsella (R) were seriously injured in the crash

“When you watch social media and you watch the responses and you hear what people are saying, that’s the result of bad actions and very often, then, in all of that, there’s so much hurt created for the family.

‌



“Sarah put it so well, she doesn’t wish any of you to walk in her shoes, to have to bury her son. There’s no great future in all of that.

“And again, as I say, the dust has settled somewhat, and the week has passed by, there is something I want to say, and especially to Jack’s friends, and it’s this – if you’re considering continuing this criminal activity, will you please stop?

“Just one word, stop. Because this is the end of it."

‌



View 4 Images Jack was one of the five teenagers who died in a motorway crash in Co Kildare earlier this month (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

“This is a family broken, and the consequences of that will happen to you too, for you yourself, for your families, the communities in which you live in, and then you’ll have the innocent victims, like the people who are in hospital trying to recover.

“There is no need for it. So again, I say to you, please, please, please, stop.”

Article continues below

One of the items brought to the altar was a car to represent Jack’s “love for cars”.

Young, Wild & Free by Snoop Dogg and Wiz Khalifa played as the coffin was taken from the chapel for a private cremation.

News.title: Mum's hands and legs amputated after routine checkup leads to nightmare
News.content:
Mum's hands and legs amputated after routine checkup leads to nightmare

A mum who went for what she thought was a routine heart check-up was left facing a devastating new reality after doctors uncovered a life-threatening condition

View 3 Images Leslie Caoili (Image: eyJpdiI6IlNjbjNvY3FRYTZnbjljRnJXaG93bHc9PSIsInZhbHVlIjoiSURrQ0s0cmtucWRxU01hNHlQT1FLcEZQQ21xelQ5R0N0UWxLdldiUktXQ1g0WXNlRWpnZ2VQcXBIazRYa1RVRFhXM0lWU1VPQVdhdXM5V1BUeGNkSHc9PSIsIm1hYyI6IjUwZDcwMzgwYjZk)

A mum who went for what she thought would be a routine heart check-up has endured a devastating turn of events after doctors discovered a life-threatening condition.

‌



Leslie Caoili, 41, from San Diego, was found to have a Type A aortic dissection, a tear in the main artery carrying blood away from the heart. She was rushed into emergency surgery, with the procedure ultimately saving her life but leaving her facing a future she could never have imagined.

‌



Leslie underwent an eight-and-a-half-hour operation involving cardiopulmonary bypass and extensive reconstruction of her aorta.

‌



We can all eat more cheese, gut health clue to Alzheimer’s, breakfast staple cuts cholesterol, and erectile dysfunction pills help you live longer - all this and more in our science newsletter

Her husband, Lee Caoili, said the seriousness of what doctors had discovered only became clear as the emergency unfolded.

“Most people who suffer an aortic dissection usually happens pretty quickly, and they don't survive. So the surgery was necessary in order to save her life. She probably had maybe hours left to live, and we wouldn't even, we didn't even know it,” he told ABC.

‌



Leslie had been a healthy, competitive strength athlete and is a mum to two daughters with Lee. But in the weeks following the operation, further complications emerged.

View 3 Images Leslie Caoili (Image: eyJpdiI6IllmSWpPU1Q1Uis2RW5reEFoQnFGVVE9PSIsInZhbHVlIjoib1NVZVUrRkdnd0xTaUh2V0d4MjZ3ek5QeGtySGhhcGl6S1NHdE9vcjZKcW5BWGFrWjV6Rno2b0wwTFVmYTUxeVZlZkowMjhSWXdidmNSejNBaXV5M1E9PSIsIm1hYyI6ImJmODJlZGJjYWRj)

She suffered severe circulation problems, with blood flow to her hands and feet becoming critically restricted.

‌



“We didn't really know how her body was gonna respond to the initial surgery, but she ended up losing blood flow to her hands and her feet, and by the end of the first month there, her hands and her feet were blackened and shriveled,” Lee said.

Doctors were eventually forced to amputate Leslie's hands at the mid-forearm, as well as both of her legs.

Lee has described the ordeal as an ongoing fight for his wife, who has spent months in hospital.

‌



“Every day has been a battle for her. Every day has been a fight,” he said.

According to the family's GoFundMe appeal, Leslie has required intensive life support during her recovery, including a ventilator, dialysis and ECMO. The fundraiser says the family is now facing mounting medical, travel, childcare and household costs, alongside the prospect of long-term rehabilitation.

The family has also been preparing for Leslie's eventual return home. Their house needs significant modifications to make it suitable for her new needs, and Lee is appealing for skilled volunteers including carpenters, electricians, roofers, flooring installers, painters and HVAC technicians.

‌



View 3 Images Leslie Caoili (Image: eyJpdiI6IkEyQUp5czVuTCtlaENNUXFKNTBrZWc9PSIsInZhbHVlIjoiK2cvSGRpblBPQkNxZmxuWGw5VHh2ZjYyYlNuTmpQM1lvM1ROUkUxRkJyTUVIM05USlZra0FqMWtNQXNoM0l1UG8rWXN3OVFHSEFjb0lYVG42YmFOZ2c9PSIsIm1hYyI6ImE1NGQ0Yzk1MjBj)

For Lee, making the property accessible is about giving his wife something she desperately wants after everything she has endured.

“She just wants to come home to her family and her kids and her dog and me and wants to get back to living life as normal as we can make it for her,” he said.

Article continues below

A GoFundMe appeal set up for Leslie's recovery has a target of $140,000, with money intended to cover medical and recovery expenses, travel and accommodation during her hospital stay, household costs and long-term rehabilitation.

The appeal describes Leslie as “a loving wife, devoted mother, daughter, sister, and friend” and says she has always been someone others could rely on.

Her family is now asking for support as they prepare for the next stage of her recovery, while hoping to make her return home as safe and comfortable as possible.

News.title: Little boy who waited a world record eight years for a new heart is back home at last
News.content:
Little boy who waited a world record eight years for a new heart is back home at last

Exclusive: Daithi MacGabhann, nine, spent more than eight years desperately hoping for the gift of life. His dad, Mairtin, joined the Mirror's crusade to change the law for life to the opt-out system introduced first in England, then in his native northern Ireland.

View 3 Images Daithi Mac Gabhann has gone home after waiting eight years for a new heart

A little boy who had a world record wait on the organ donor list has finally returned home - with his new heart beating under his Liverpool shirt.

‌



Daithi Mac Gabhann is nine years old and spent more than eight years desperately hoping for the gift of life. His dad, Mairtin, 36, joined the Mirror's crusade to change the law in his native Northern Ireland to the opt-out system introduced in England following our 'Change the Law for Life' campaign.

‌



In 2023, the Northern Irish assembly passed Daithi's law, which brought organ donation rules there into line with the rest of the UK. Daitha had been waiting for the transplant call since 2018.

‌



He was under the care of the same Freeman Hospital children's transplant team that looked after Mirror campaigner Max Johnson, now 18 and at college.

View 3 Images Daithi Mac Gabhann spent more than eight years desperately hoping for the gift of life, a world record.

Daithi left Ward 23 to a guard of honour and the sound of the Rocky anthem, "Eye of the Tiger." He remained on Tyneside for a few more weeks as he continued his recovery.

‌



But he has now flown back to Ireland, arriving back on Monday evening, wearing the home shirt of his beloved Liverpool FC. His family posted images of him arriving in Belfast after the short 45-minute flight from Newcastle.

He was required to travel with a small number of family members as he has to remain in isolation as much as he can while taking anti-rejection drugs for his new donor heart.

He travelled on an air ambulance, thanking the staff who cared for him as he made his way home. Mairtin has vowed to continue to raise awareness of the importance of organ donation.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He is back home. Everything happened so suddenly on Monday. He got back on Monday evening and it is great to be back."

He added: "Everyone has heard of Daithi now back in Ireland, so the law change is a massive part of our society now. But we are also learning from some of the mistakes with opt-out. We have to keep the pressure on politicians to make it work."

View 3 Images Daithi Mac Gabhann arriving back home after his world record eight year wait for a new heart

‌



His son will now be able to "make the absolute most of life" thanks to his transplant. "We always knew he had freckles, but I mean you want to see how popping these freckles are. It's just unbelievable," he said.

Mairtin and his wife Seph, 30, who also have two-year-old twins Padraig, Declan and son Cairbre, four, worked tirelessly to introduce a new organ donor legislation in Northern Ireland.

It was named Daithi's Law in honour of his son, and introduced in Northern Ireland in 2023, three years after the Mirror backed Max and Keira's Law was introduced in England.

‌



"We met Max and his family at the British Heart Foundation awards and have kept in touch," Mairtin recalled. "Max is doing well and the story of Max and Keira gave us hope.

"They are our heroes and increased Daithi's chances of getting a heart. The Mirror campaign has done so much to raise awareness, we are truly grateful for that."

Mairtin was made an MBE in 2024. Daithi was awarded the freedom of Belfast in 2023, also for his work on the organ donation campaign.

‌



His dad added: "Organ donation is the greatest gift anyone can ever give. We are beyond grateful to Daithi's donor and their family for making such a selfless decision at the most difficult time imaginable."

Mirror campaigner Max, of Winsford, Cheshire, insisted Keira, who died aged nine in a car accident near her home in Barnstaple, Devon, should be remembered forever when the new law was named in their honour.

He thinks of Keira every Christmas, birthday and anniversary of his operation, which took place in August, 2017. He said: "I will be forever grateful."

‌



Max and Keira's Law means adults in England are now considered to be organ donors when they die unless they 'opt out'. It was introduced in May, 2020.

It also means would-be donors no longer need to carry a donor card. Both adult and child patients can wait years for an organ transplant.

In 2018, Gareth Evans, 45, a dad-of-two from Stockport, made a public appeal for donors after more than nine years waiting for a new heart.

‌



He originally had a heart transplant in 1990 for cardiomyopathy, when he was aged just 17, but it was failing. “Having a new heart is like being a little boy and having Christmas every day," he said at the time.

"But having to tell the family you may not make it, is the most difficult thing to do. The final thing you can do is to be a hero, save people's lives. There's nothing more marvellous than that."

He received a new heart in October, 2018, but sadly died days later.

Article continues below
