News.title: Father's house rammed before son died in A66 crash
News.content:
A house rammed by a car before the fatal A66 crash in Middlesbrough belonged to the father of a teenager who died in the incident.

Cole Worthy, 17, was one of five young men who died when a Volkswagen Passat travelling in the wrong direction hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle, also killing two police officers.

Before the crash at 03:39 BST on Saturday, police had received multiple reports of two cars driving dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60 was seen ramming properties.

The BBC understands that, after his father's home was rammed, Worthy and the four others set out in the Passat. Police said they were linking the activities of the Volvo XC60 and the Passat.

There is no suggestion Worthy's father was involved in criminal activity.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Worthy.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said officers had been pursuing the Passat for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when it turned on to the dual carriageway.

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.

News.title: Who does Iran trade with and what could Trump's 'economic D-Day' mean?
News.content:
The US has said "the single greatest financial offensive ever" will help it and Israel end their ongoing war with Iran.

However, Iran is no stranger to these tactics.

The regime has faced near continuous US sanctions since the Islamic Revolution of 1979. In that time, it has developed deep trade ties with several countries which either have a history of ignoring US economic pressure themselves or cannot afford to stop trading with Iran.

As a result, Iran says it is "fully prepared" for the new US sanctions and many economists argue the impact of Washington's latest move will be limited.

So, who does Iran trade with? And could what the US has called an "economic D-Day" have any real impact on Iran?

News.title: Man dies in crash after police pursuit
News.content:
A man has died and two women have been injured in a crash after a police pursuit near Stratford-upon-Avon.

Officers tried to stop a black Audi on Birmingham Road shortly before 17:30 BST on Monday but the driver failed to pull over, Warwickshire Police said.

A pursuit began and 15 minutes later the Audi crashed into a white Ford Puma, the force added, with the Audi's 19-year-old male driver confirmed dead at the scene by paramedics.

The driver of the Ford, a woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital in critical condition, while injuries to a second woman - her passenger - were serious but not believed to be life-threatening. An investigation by the police watchdog is under way.

Officers said after failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road where the crash occurred.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

Warwick Road was closed on Monday from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane, with the stretch remaining shut on Tuesday morning.

It has since reopened.

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued as thunderstorms and flooding forecast
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.

The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.

It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.

While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.

News.title: Young people leaving care have death rate four times higher than national average
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: US judge rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's 'frivolous' appeal against conviction
News.content:
Ghislaine Maxwell's latest bid to overturn her sex trafficking conviction has been rejected by a US judge, who dismissed her claims as "frivolous" and "meritless".

The 64-year-old is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her role in procuring girls for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein after being found guilty in December 2021.

Maxwell had appealed against her five felony convictions, claiming her constitutional rights had been "violated in multiple respects".

But a New York judge flatly rejected the appeal, describing it as "lengthy and rambling".

Maxwell said Epstein-related documents released by the US Justice Department earlier this year supported her case that she had been wrongly convicted.

But the judge ruled that "far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness" of her conviction.

The judge also said her appeal "falls very far from the mark", adding: "Nearly all its claims are procedurally barred; the overwhelming testimonial and documentary evidence adduced at trial conclusively established her guilt; and her petition's claims are demonstrably meritless, and generally based on speculation, distortions, and/or outright falsehoods.

"There is no fact that Maxwell fairly puts in dispute that has any potential to disturb the outcome of her trial."

The judge warned Maxwell against making further appeals, saying it "would not be taken in good faith" by the court.

Maxwell was found guilty in 2021 of facilitating Epstein's abuse. Prosecutors said she recruited and groomed girls, some as young as 14, between 1994 and 2004, before they were abused by Epstein, who died in prison in 2019.

Maxwell appeared virtually before the US House Oversight Committee in February this year but refused to answer questions, invoking her right to remain silent as she pleaded the Fifth Amendment.

Republican House Oversight Committee chairman James Comer said the situation was "very disappointing", adding: "We had many questions to ask about the crimes she and Epstein committed, as well as questions about potential co-conspirators."

Maxwell has previously sought a pardon from US President Donald Trump.

When asked last October whether he would consider pardoning Maxwell, Trump said he "wouldn't consider it or not consider it", adding: "I don't know anything about it, so I will speak to the [Department of Justice]."

The US Senate last month passed a resolution declaring its opposition to a presidential pardon for Maxwell.

News.title: Inspectors to assess police after Henry Nowak murder
News.content:
An inspection into how a police force responds to violent incidents has been launched in the wake of Henry Nowak's murder.

The 18-year-old student was stabbed in Southampton by Vickrum Digwa, who lied to police and insisted he had been the victim of a racist attack.

Hampshire Police officers initially arrested Nowak and placed him in handcuffs as he lay dying.

His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Service (HMICFRS) will assess the force's processes, training and how officers are supported to make sound and impartial judgements.

The inspection was requested by Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones, who said the public "must have confidence" in the force.

"This inspection will provide an independent assessment of the force's training, processes and culture, including the handling of allegations of racially aggravated assault," she said.

"Henry's family deserve answers, and the public deserve reassurance that their police service is equipped to recognise victims and provide the highest standard of care when it matters most."

News.title: Andrew Tate exaggerates and did not own supercars in photos, his lawyers say
News.content:
Controversial influencer Andrew Tate portrays himself as "uberwealthy" but did not own cars and a yacht featured on his social media and exaggerated his lifestyle for online attention, his legal representatives have said.

Tate and his brother Tristan are currently being held in a Florida jail but are seeking release on bail while they await the outcome of extradition proceedings.

They were arrested last month after British prosecutors unveiled new charges including alleged sexual offences against them, which both men deny.

Prosecutors have argued the Tates are a "flight risk", citing the brothers' past statements about their wealth and influence and having multiple identities to evade the law.

In a legal submission to the court, the brothers' legal representatives said the Tates' business model "depends on online attention".

"The outrageousness of the posts by them and about them is the point. The more hyperbolic and outlandish the post, the more likely it will generate views and likes, which in turn generates income. In short, they are playing a role," it says.

At times Andrew Tate has also exaggerated and used hyperbole for "comedic effect" with no intention to be taken seriously, the submission argues.

"The government alleges that the Tates are a risk of flight based on their social media claims that they are 'self-proclaimed billionaires' who own 'high-end vehicles, private jets, and a custom $50-million-dollar superyacht and have unrestricted access to traditional funds, cryptocurrency, and bitcoin,'" it says.

"But the government has not established these grandiose claims are true," it adds.

News.title: Boy, 3, injured in crocodile attack returns home
News.content:
A three-year-old boy who was seriously injured in a crocodile enclosure has been discharged from hospital and is settling back in at home, his family has said.

The child returned home "a few weeks ago" and is "happy to be home, playing with his toys, sleeping in his own bed and being a big brother", his parents said in an update posted online.

The boy was visiting Johnsons of Old Hurst near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, with his family on 18 June when he was attacked by at least one of the animals.

In an update shared on a fundraising page on Monday, the boy's family said it was "nice to have us all back together in the comfort of our own home".

Cambridgeshire Police arrested and bailed a 30-year-old man from Norfolk on suspicion of attempted murder after the incident.

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Tributes have been led by prime minister Andy Burnham who said he was a "giant of a man in every way".

"Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died," he said on social media.

"Billy was one of the greatest rugby league players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet.

"He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan.

"I will miss him greatly and am thinking today of Billy's family, still grieving the recent loss of his beloved wife Joan."

Wigan owner Mike Danson said: "Billy Boston was everybody's hero, including my mum's.

"His achievements in rugby league were extraordinary, and his knighthood was a fitting recognition of a career that brought great credit to Wigan and to the game.

"But Billy's legacy was not simply what he achieved. It was the humility with which he carried it. Despite everything he accomplished, he remained a quiet, dignified and deeply respected man.

"He leaves behind an example that will endure for generations. Our thoughts are with his family and those closest to him.

"A great man, and a true Wigan legend. He will be remembered with pride and affection."

In a statement, Wales Rugby League said: "Today, rugby league has lost one of its greatest-ever players, Wales has lost one of its finest sporting sons, and our sport has lost a truly special gentleman."

The WRU also paid tribute, calling Boston "one of the best loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport".

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy added: "He was, in my view, the greatest rugby league player of all time and one of the nicest people I've ever had the privilege to know."

News.title: 'We just want to get home' - dozens stranded in Tunisia after cancelled Belfast flight
News.content:
Dozens of people from Northern Ireland have been left stranded in Tunisia after their EasyJet flight back to Belfast was cancelled and the airline told them it had no other flights available for another 10 days.

A number of people have scrambled for alternative journeys back to Northern Ireland, with one man saying he has spent more than Â£4,000 to get his family of five home.

Some told BBC News NI of passengers running out of medication since the cancellation on Saturday, while others criticised EasyJet over a lack of support and communication.

EasyJet has said it is operating an additional direct flight to Belfast on Tuesday night, and that it was "very sorry" for the inconvenience.

BBC News NI understands more than 100 people were booked onto the cancelled flight that was due to leave Enfidha-Hamamet Airport three days ago.

Stuart McCartney, from Dromore, County Down, said he had spent thousands on accommodation and flights to get his family home via a flight to Brussels.

"I'm willing to pay Â£4,000 to get us home, if needs be, and then battle for reimbursement if I have to after that," he said.

"But we shouldn't have to pay. My holiday was a fraction of what I'm paying to get home right now."

McCartney said EasyJet provided two nights of accommodation but then told the family to find alternative accommodation for the rest of the delay.

He said his mother Katherine, who accompanied his wife and children on the trip, relies on heart medication and they have had to keep a close eye on her remaining supply as the delay continued.

An EasyJet spokesperson said they were "very sorry" that the flight had been cancelled and that the company "have been doing everything we can to support Mr McCartney, providing hotel accommodation and meals and we will be reimbursing expenses that may have been incurred".

Another woman, Martine Murray, said she had run out of an inhaler to treat her COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease) and is anxious to get home to her mother, who is seriously ill.

Chloe McGinty, a student from County Donegal, said it had been "an absolute nightmare".

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Housing charities welcomed the news but said it was still not enough to meet demand, while the Conservatives said it was an "unfunded spending commitment".

Social housing provides affordable homes at a low cost, managed by social landlords. It includes affordable rented properties as well as low-cost home ownership, such as shared ownership, and can be provided by local authorities and housing associations.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing Minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Man guilty of killing student after fake Rolex row
News.content:
A student who stabbed his former friend through the heart in Leicester after they fell out over a fake Rolex watch has been found guilty of manslaughter.

Harper Dennis, 19, plunged a knife five times into the chest of Khaleed Oladipo, 20, near De Montfort University in Leicester on the evening of February 3 this year.

A jury at Leicester Crown Court found Dennis not guilty of murder but guilty of manslaughter, having an offensive weapon and failing to provide the pin to his phone after a two-week trial.

Dennis, of Bath Lane, Leicester, was told he would be sentenced later on Tuesday.

Prosecutor Jane Osborne KC told the jury Dennis killed Oladipo, who he made friends with through online gaming, because of a "perceived debt".

The trial heard their friendship soured after an unsuccessful attempt by Dennis to sell a fake Rolex given to him by Oladipo.

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

News.title: Man convicted after being caught on CCTV upskirting girl in shopping centre
News.content:
A man has pleaded guilty to filming beneath a young girl's skirt in a shopping centre before running off and later being tracked down on CCTV.

Alex Allegretto, 39, admitted the offence of operating a mobile phone beneath the clothing of another person for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification.

Police were called to St David's 2 shopping centre on the morning of 7 July after a mother reported Allegretto, who was unknown to them, for upskirting her daughter.

He was caught on CCTV heading back to his car and was later arrested for voyeurism at his home in Maesteg, in Bridgend County Borough.

Allegretto was sentenced at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on 5 August.

The CCTV footage shows Allegretto sat on a bench before quickly walking up behind the victim and her mum in the busy shopping centre and putting his phone by her legs before running away.

Sgt Luis Antony, from South Wales Police, said the victim had continued to be impacted by the incident.

"She is worried about people walking behind her and is anxious when out and about," he added.

Antony said that "nobody should be subjected to this kind of offence".

"The footage clearly shows Alex Allegretto's intentions and what he did to this young girl while she was innocently out shopping with her mother," he added.

"We hope the outcome at court provides some comfort to her and allows her to rebuild her confidence."

The court heard that Allegretto must be registered with the police in accordance with the Sexual Offences Act 2003 , externalfor five years.

He must also do 140 hours of unpaid work, complete rehabilitation activity requirements and pay a financial penalty of Â£199.

News.title: New 10p coin enters circulation - will you spot one?
News.content:
Something new might appear in your change when you pay in cash from now on: a 10p coin featuring the portrait of King Charles and the world's largest grouse.

Sufficient demand for the coins mean newly-minted 10p pieces are entering circulation for the first time for about four years, this time with a new design.

The Royal Mint says shoppers and collectors should discover the coins, which were minted and dated in 2023 and 2026, across the country.

The reverse side of the coin depicts an image of the capercaillie which is found in a small part of Scotland and threatened with extinction.

The redesigned suite of coins to celebrate the King's love of the natural world were unveiled in October 2023 by The Royal Mint.

The tails side of every newly-minted coin from the 1p to the Â£2 now features the country's flora and fauna - from bees to an oak tree leaf.

Coins in circulation in the UK carrying the portrait of King Charles have so far been limited to the 5p, 50p and Â£1.

Old coins with the image of the late Queen Elizabeth II can still be used, so the new coins are only struck in response to demand.

That is why, with 1.4 billion 10p coins in circulation, there has been no need for the new 10p to be released until now by The Royal Mint.

Now. 600,000 of these coins, dated 2023, and 6.5 million dated 2026 have been released to banks and post offices nationwide.

However, King Charles III coins still only represent about 1% of the 24.1 billion coins in circulation across the UK, making any new ones highly sought after by seasoned numismatists and new coin collectors.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal make Barcola decision, huge Man Utd boost, Alvarez latest
News.content:
Alvarez kicks off a last week of big transfer sagas

Arsenal are hoping to secure the signing of Julian Alvarez to cap off a productive summer of incomings and boost their forward line as they look to defend their Premier League title. Alvarez is said to be open to the move having initially favoured a switch to Barcelona.

Liverpool’s pursuit of PSG’s Bradley Barcola was given a boost when he was left out of the squad for their game against Rennes with PSG insiders now expecting the winger to leave the clubs this summer. The Reds have also seen two bids for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh turned down.

Elsewhere, Manchester City have agreed a €100m deal with Lille to buy midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi and have sold Savinho to Tottenham in a deal worht £85m. They are also interested in Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo. Across the city, Manchester United target Alejandro Balde reportedly wants to leave Barcelona with the Premier League club exploring a loan move for the left-back.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez were also absent from Aston Villa’s matchday squad amid rumours that both players could be preparing for imminent exits with Watkins’ in particular looking very close to a move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal.

Carlos Baleba has joined Manchester United as Michael Carrick has completed a hat-trick of midfield buys this season.

The Cameroon international, who has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford, has joined from Brighton for an initial £65m.

United could pay an extra £5m in add-ons for the 22-year-old, who believes he can reach a new level under Carrick, a former midfielder.

Carlos Baleba has signed for Manchester United from Brighton and Hove Albion ( Manchester United )

Baleba said: “It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

Baleba joins Andrey Santos, a £48m buy from Chelsea, and Youri Tielemans, a £35m arrival from Aston Villa, in a £148m overhaul of the United midfield.

United were first interested in him last summer, following an excellent 2024-25 season, and while he had a tougher season last year, they still wanted him.

United director of football Jason Wilcox said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

“Carlos’ determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.”

Tadej Pogacar produced another peerless performance as he soloed to victory from 50km from the finish on the mountainous fourth stage of the Vuelta a Espana.

The Slovenian, who is riding the Vuelta for only the second time in his career and for the first time in seven years, was the overwhelming pre-race favourite and had been widely expected to put the competition to bed in the opening week.

Stage three’s cancellation due to severe hailstorms prevented him from making a late raid on the final climb to Font Romeu and delivering that statement of intent.

But he made up for lost time on stage four, attacking on the second of three category-one climbs, the Collada de Beixalis. None of his rivals had any response to his acceleration on the 6.5km, 8.5% climb, and they were left scrapping among themselves for the minor places over the remaining 50km.

Victory in Andorra la Vella marked his longest solo victory at a grand tour, at the only one of the three which he is left to win, and his second in four days, having claimed victory and the leader’s jersey on stage one’s individual time trial.

Pogacar said afterwards: “I didn’t have to do that, but the pace was super high already on the first climb, then on the second climb we were going all-out from the bottom, then when Jay [Vine, his teammate] let me pass from the wheel of Decathlon I thought I don’t want to be also isolated against all these GC riders because they would go against me.

“I tried an attack and hoped I could survive until the finish. It was pretty tough but beautiful out there.

“Any gap is more than enough but it’s super good because now I can be calm and confident for the next days.”

Asked about his memories of first ever grand tour stage win, which came in the 2019 edition of the Vuelta and in Andorra, he said: “I never thought that I would ride like this, I have such beautiful memories from the first time in Andorra, it’s one of my favourite moments of the career so I will never forget that day.”

Stage four was a punchy 104.8km run starting and beginning in Andorra la Vella and tackling four climbs: three category-one ascents in a row before a final category three. As many of the peloton are based in the mountainous principality the route covered familiar terrain, but they were still powerless to respond to Monaco resident Pogacar once he accelerated away.

open image in gallery Pogacar now leads the overall standings by more than three minutes ( Reuters )

The two-time world champion extended his advance over the next category-one climb, the 9.9km Coll d'Ordino, while behind him, Giro d’Italia runner-up Felix Gall attacked with 33km to go.

Initially only Netcompany-Ineos’ Oscar Onley was able to follow his wheel, but four-time Vuelta champion Primoz Roglic bridged across 3km later and the trio were soon joined by more elite climbers in the form of home favourite Enric Mas and 2023 champion Sepp Kuss.

That group swelled to seven by the finish line, with 20-year-old Jarno Widar of Lotto Intermarche, one of the peloton’s most exciting young talents, winning the sprint for second from Decathlon CMA CGM’s Gall, two minutes and 39 seconds down on Pogacar.

24-year-old Onley was fourth on the stage - all the more impressive given he admitted afterwards he had “been up all night on the toilet” - and now leads the best young riders’ classification.

The Scot cut a deflated figure afterwards and said of Pogacar, “We just let him do our thing, and race between ourselves.”

UAE Team Emirates-XRG’s Pogacar now leads the Vuelta by 3’21” from compatriot Roglic, who won the race the last time Pogacar competed, with Mas third another 11 seconds back. Kuss sits fourth at 3’44” and Onley fifth at 3’45”.

President Donald Trump has ordered further work on the South Lawn of the White House where his new helipad is being built, calling for the garden’s entire slope to be leveled out, according to a report.

Construction crews have been seen in recent days tearing up huge portions of earth in order to bring the lawn flush with the helipad, a task Trump has demanded be finished in time for Chinese Premier Xi Jinping’s arrival on September 24.

“The lawn will gently be reshaped to meet the new helipad,” an unnamed White House official told The Washington Post.

The president first announced the helipad’s construction in early July, explaining that a new fleet of Sikorsky Aircraft helicopters delivered to the White House in 2024 had encountered a problem: their exhaust vents aim heat downwards when they land and take off, burning the grass.

open image in gallery Construction work ongoing on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, D.C., after President Donald Trump raised objections to the extent of its slope ( Getty )

Trump has continued to use the previous Marine One fleet instead of the new VH‑92A Patriot models and said that Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin subsidiary, is paying the $6 million cost of the helipad because, he said, they “felt a little bit guilty” about the issue created.

The president had to wait until his birthday UFC bout on June 14 had been completed before the project could commence but personally chose the white granite being used, hailing it as “the strongest stone.”

However, within a month the work completed was already having to be redone – including the dismantling of a 100-foot-wide presidential seal – after Trump complained that the sloping lawn meant the helipad would not be sitting level with the horizon.

“For years, the White House has desperately needed a proper helipad on White House grounds that will allow the president to land safely and also protect the beautiful South Lawn grass from the fierce exhaust fumes of the incredible Marine One,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle previously told The Independent.

“Thanks to President Trump, the White House has never looked better, and it will only continue to get better under his leadership.”

open image in gallery The work has already had to be torn up and redone once in accordance with the president’s exacting specificiations ( Getty )

Trump invited the Washington press corps on a tour of the construction site last Wednesday, praising the workers involved as “real artists.”

The time slot had been set aside for a “policy meeting” but Trump instead could be found out in the sun, telling reporters in characteristic style: “I was very good at real estate, like maybe the best in a lot of ways, and I love construction. I love seeing things properly taken care of.”

He also addressed his dissatisfaction with the lawn. “We had a lot of slope on it, and I felt it was too much slope,” the president said.

He added the helipad would be “much better for state arrivals” and suggested: “ They can have events on it. They can have people go there for cocktails and then walk to the ballroom.”

Trump was back at the site Monday with a group of children taking part in a “back to school” event, insisting: “Kids love construction.”

open image in gallery Trump is set to welcome China's President Xi Jinping next month ( AFP/Getty )

The project is just one of numerous embellishments the president has made to the White House and the surrounding area in Washington, D.C., since returning to power last year.

The most prominent remains the massive $600m ballroom he hopes to erect in place of the demolished East Wing, which has been the subject of a prolonged legal battle. Its fate currently rests with the Supreme Court.

Other signature Trump enterprises include paving over the Rose Garden to turn it into a Florida patio, adding new plaques and signage across 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue and, most disastrously, making over the Lincoln Memorial’s Reflecting Pool in “American Flag Blue.”

All together, the cost of the president’s projects has been pegged at $927 million so far.

New York Times journalist Maggie Haberman estimated in her recent book Regime Change, co-written with colleague Jonathan Swan, that Trump devotes around 70 percent of his focus to his “beautifying” agenda, leaving only 30 percent for such pressing concerns as the Iran war, the domestic economy and November’s midterm elections.

The editor-in-chief of CBS News wants to add fired CNN anchor Chris Cuomo to the network’s lineup of stars, according to a report.

​Bari Weiss has overseen significant changes since she was appointed to the role in October, with a number of high profile figures leaving including former 60 Minutes stalwart Anderson Cooper.

In a bid to attract more big-name talent, the editor-in-chief is in talks with Cuomo to join the network, sources told Status.

​Oliver Darcy, a journalist at the publication, said Weiss was “enraptured” by Cuomo and had already met him in person. The pair, he reports, met for a meal and have often swapped text messages.

If a deal did go ahead, Cuomo would join CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil as another high-profile Weiss appointee.

open image in gallery Bari Weiss reportedly wants to add Chris Cuomo to CBS News' lineup ( Getty )

However one potential obstacle is Cuomo’s current contract with NewsNation, which announced in 2024 it had signed a multi-year deal with the former CNN anchor. ​Cuomo also launched Cuomo Mornings on SiriusXM just this year, with the live show featuring guests including Senator Rand Paul.

The Independent has contacted CBS News for comment.

While Cuomo has yet to comment on the potential career move, he did this week shoot down a suggestion he could join NBC News’ Meet the Press.

“I would be very different but I would not do it,” he wrote on X Sunday. “There is a farce at play on the sunday shows...transparency and accountability are very difficult to achieve.”

Cuomo was fired by CNN back in 2021 for helping his brother, ex-Governor of New York Andrew Cuomo, after the latter was accused of sexual assault.​ Andrew Cuomo has denied all wrongdoing.

“This is not how I want my time at CNN to end, but I have already told you why and how I helped my brother,” he said in a statement at the time.​

open image in gallery Weiss (pictured) became editor-in-chief of CBS News after its parent company merged with David Ellison's firm ( Getty )

Weiss’ appointment last year followed a merger of Paramount Global, CBS News’ parent company, and Skydance Media, which was founded by billionaire and Trump ally David Ellison.

Since then, critics have accused her of steering coverage to favor the Trump administration, leading to backlash from current and former staff.

​Former 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley was fired by the program’s executive producer Nick Bilton after reportedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the news program.

​Weiss has denied the claims of editorial interference and in June she told The Wall Street Journal she was just doing her job.

​“What’s being called ‘editorial interference’ is in reality the job description of an editor in chief,” Weiss said.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.

Sports.content:
Ashley Cole leaves England U21 set-up after five years and sets sight on new role

The Football Association have confirmed that former Arsenal and England defender Ashley Cole has left his position with the national team's Under-21s

View 2 Images Ashley Cole is looking for a club role after leaving the England U21s (Image: Nathan Stirk/Getty Images)

Ashley Cole has left his role with England under-21s after five years as a coach.

‌



Former England defender Cole was part of under-21s boss Lee Carsley’s coaching staff which won back-to-back European titles. Cole retired from his playing career in 2019 and moved into coaching and it is believed he wants to carry on at club level.

‌



Carsley said Cole had a “positive, inspirational impact on his players” and added: “I want to pay tribute to Ashley who played a major part in our two Euro wins and also had a key role in the current campaign with his tactical and technical knowledge.

‌



“I am certain he will have even more success in his coaching career whatever the future holds.”

Cole worked under Frank Lampard at Derby, had a spell at Chelsea ’s academy and then was assistant manager at Everton and Birmingham.

‌



The ex-Arsenal and Chelsea left back is one of England’s all-time great defenders and he had a recent spell as head coach of Serie B club Cesena in March after not getting a chance in his own right in English football.

But Cole, who won 107 caps and three Premier League titles and a European Cup during his glorious playing career, left Cesena in June, citing a “change in the club's strategy.”

Cole took to social media to explain his departure, writing: “As my tenure at Cesena FC concludes today, I want to thank the players and staff for their hard work and commitment over the last few months.

‌

“I was proud to bring my experience to such a passionate club, and I’ve truly enjoyed working with the squad to introduce a new identity and prepare for the season ahead.

“Following recent discussions with the Sporting Director regarding a change in the club’s strategy, I have decided that it is best for me to move on.

“I leave with great respect for all the people there, as well as the fans, and look forward to my next challenge.”

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez is Premier League's public enemy No.1 after striking Fulham reaction
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez is Premier League's public enemy No.1 after striking Fulham reaction

Enzo Fernandez was heavily jeered by Fulham supporters at Craven Cottage during his first appearance for Chelsea since reaffirming his pantomime villain status with Argentina at the World Cup

View 3 Images Manchester City remain keen to sign Enzo Fernandez (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Enzo Fernandez is now officially the Premier League’s public enemy No.1. The Chelsea midfielder was jeered, booed and taunted at Craven Cottage during his first appearance since the World Cup.

‌



This was not your normal smattering of chants. A few fans. No, it was loud and vicious. They chanted “England” and booed his every touch. We are talking the latte-sipping classes at Fulham here. Quaint Craven Cottage. It was quite remarkable and overwhelming. Not just a few boos.

‌



And it was a taste of things to come in every game this season. Football fans up and down the country will not forgive Fernandez for his part in Argentina’s ugly, bad-tempered and bitter win over England in the World Cup semi-final. And, in particular, the way Fernandez taunted England fans afterwards by cupping his hands to his ears to mock them after Argentina’s victory in Atlanta.

‌



And that makes it rather hard to understand why Fernandez seems intent on moving from Chelsea to Manchester City. City boss Enzo Maresca wants to sign Fernandez, the player he managed and coached at Chelsea. Chelsea are braced for a £120million from City this week.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



So, Fernandez will swap one Premier League club for another. It begs the question: why on earth not just move abroad? That would stop it.

Well, one answer is obviously that no major European team is ready to pay the transfer fee - or probably match his wages. Fernandez made himself unpopular with Chelsea fans last season by flirting with Real Madrid - only for the Spanish giants to come out publicly and say they were not interested.

That left Chelsea fans split on Fernandez and yet, actually, they chanted his name on Monday night to support him. Mind you, that was probably as much of a reaction to Fulham’s noise as anything else. In their heart of hearts, Chelsea fans don’t much like him either.

‌



You could see even the Chelsea bench were a bit bemused by it all. One or two, including Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, were chuckling away. Whether we like it or not, it will be a theme of the season. Of course we’ve had it before.

Many years ago, Ricky Villa and Ossie Ardiles faced a backlash because of the Falklands War. Ardiles went to Paris Saint Germain on loan. But he was quickly welcomed back. Cristiano Ronaldo got some heat after the 2006 World Cup when he got Wayne Rooney sent off after Portugal beat England in the quarter-final.

Should Manchester City sign Enzo Fernandez? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez received an unwelcome reception at Fulham (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Even Arsenal’s Ben White got some stick after quitting the England camp in the Qatar World Cup in 2022. There are plenty of other examples. Blimey, Chelsea do not appear to care as they signed Valentín Barco even though the Argentinian taunted England hero Jude Bellingham after the game.

Fernandez clearly feeds off the anger and animosity. He is quite a character. That is to be admired. But the reality is that he is really not that special. He works hard, has an incredible determination and spirit while he also plays for Argentina, one of the best teams in world football. His engine is better than his finesse.

‌



Has Fernandez really justified his £106m price tag from when he joined Chelsea in 2023? No one could quite understand it then and Argentina had just won the World Cup! And he still divides opinion now.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca wants to reunite with Enzo Fernandez (Image: Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

In fairness, Maresca got the best out of him as Chelsea won a European trophy, got back into the Champions League and won the Club World Cup. But is he really a player that would improve the best City team? He might do right now because they have lost Pep Guardiola and an army of talent.

‌



However, he will come with a warning: he will get dog’s abuse in every game he plays this season whether it is for Chelsea or City. It will surely be good business for Chelsea if they get in excess of £120m and maybe it will be fun for such a pantomime villain to remain in English football.

At least he will never go through a game unnoticed anymore (as he often tends to at Chelsea). You will know every time he touches the ball.

Sports.title: Man Utd face major Alejandro Balde transfer issue as they search for Lewis Hall alternative
Sports.content:
Man Utd face major Alejandro Balde transfer issue as they search for Lewis Hall alternative

Manchester United want to add a left-back to their squad before the summer transfer window closes for business on September 1 and have identified Alejandro Balde as a target

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is available from Barcelona (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

Manchester United have been offered the chance to sign Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde, but are reportedly unwilling to pay the asking price.

‌



United remain in the hunt to sign a left-back before the summer transfer window closes on September 1. Their initial number one target Lewis Hall now appears to be out of reach, with Newcastle unwilling to discuss a deal after selling a handful of other stars.

‌



That has led United to move onto other options, with manager Michael Carrick still keen to bring in competition for Luke Shaw, who is in his 13th season at the club and has historically suffered with injuries. United's dreadful performance in a 2-0 defeat by newly-promoted Hull on Saturday has further underlined the need for new arrivals.

‌



Balde was left out of the Barcelona squad for their 5-0 thrashing of Elche on Sunday and the 22-year-old could soon be on the move. “I spoke with Balde and told him that, in my opinion, he is not 100 per cent ready," manager Hansi Flick said. "That he should sort out his thoughts, and then we will discuss it.”

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Athletic reports that, while Barca are open to selling, they value Balde, who has nearly two years left on his contract, at €45million (£38.5m). That is too much for United, who would instead look for an initial loan deal.

Balde came through the Barcelona academy and has made 168 appearances since making his debut in 2021. He is understood to want assurances of game time if he is to stay at the club for the 2026/27 campaign.

United's hopes of finding a left-back could rely on Jorge Mendes, who represents both Balde and another target, Jorge Salinas. The 19-year-old Racing Santander defender has a release clause of just €16m (£13.6m) in his contract, but is also in talks with Atletico Madrid.

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Salinas is another possible target for Manchester United (Image: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

As well as Shaw, United have other options in the form of Patrick Dorgu, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui. However, Dorgu has been deployed on the left wing by Carrick, while Dalot and Mazraoui are more comfortable at right-back. Academy graduate Harry Amass has been made available for another loan spell away from the club.

Left-back is the last remaining piece of the puzzle for United this summer after they struck an agreement to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton for a fee which could reach £70m. The Cameroon international is set to be announced after undergoing a medical over the weekend and will join Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in a new-look midfield.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup third-round draw explained including 'pre-draw' for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup third-round draw explained including 'pre-draw' for Premier League giants

European fixtures for several Premier League sides has thrown the next round of the Carabao Cup into chaos, forcing the EFL to get creative with the upcoming draw

View 2 Images The Carabao Cup third-round draw is set to take place this week (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

The EFL have been forced to adapt the draw for the third round of the Carabao Cup after European fixtures threw a major spanner in the works.

‌



The draw will take place on Wednesday evening, following the conclusion of Preston vs Everton, on Sky Sports. It will come before all the second-round ties are concluded, with Chelsea vs Luton and Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon both taking place on Thursday night.

‌



That is just one minor confusion. It is the eight Premier League sides who are set to compete in the Champions League or Europa League this season which makes things difficult for the EFL.

‌



Arsenal, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United are all in the Champions League, while Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and Sunderland will feature in the Europa League. Brighton could still qualify for the Conference League via the qualifiers, that competition doesn't begin until October so won't clash.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Fixtures for the Champions League and Europa League in September, set for the week beginning September 7 and September 14 respectively, will clash with the third round of the Carabao Cup. The EFL have therefore decided to introduce new conditions for the draw to ensure that the aforementioned clubs cannot face each other in the third round.

They have also introduced a "pre-draw", which will take place on Sky Sports before Preston vs Everton. That will be used to determined whether the Premier League sides involved in European competitions will be drawn at home or away in the main draw.

The EFL explained in a statement: "In the main draw, to be conducted after the round two tie, the first eight ties will involve those Champions League and Europa League clubs, with their home or away position already having been decided, and each will be drawn against a club from a separate bowl containing the remaining teams. Once those eight ties have been drawn, the final eight ties will be drawn as normal."

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City won last season's Carabao Cup (Image: 2026 Allstar)

The highlights of round two include Nottingham Forest vs Leeds, Southampton vs West Ham, Newcastle vs West Brom and Tottenham vs Charlton.

Manchester City are the defending champions in the competition, having beaten Arsenal 2-0 at Wembley back in February thanks to two goals from Nico O'Reilly.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign - and the Xabi Alonso era - with a 3-2 win over Fulham, but Robert Sanchez's performance in goal left a lot to be desired

View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has encouraged Robert Sanchez to "relax and carry on" despite his dreadful start to the Premier League season.

‌



The Blues picked up a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all scoring at Craven Cottage. But while their attack looked impressive, there was an obvious issue at the other end.

‌



Sanchez was beaten at his near post by Josh King's low effort and he was also at fault for Fulham's second goal, pushing out a shot for Gonzalo Garcia to head in a rebound.

‌



The Spanish goalkeeper's erratic performances are nothing new, with mistakes a feature of his three-year Chelsea career. But Alonso refused to criticise his goalkeeper when speaking to reporters post-match.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about the team, it's not about the individual," Alonso said when asked about Sanchez's mistakes. "The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn. This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything. The goal was to start good, and we've been able to start well. Relax and carry on."

Sanchez has been Chelsea's number one goalkeeper since joining for £20million from Brighton three years ago. He has made 112 appearances, keeping his place in the side in spite of Chelsea's busy nature in the transfer market.

‌



View 2 Images Xabi Alonso dismissed concerns about his goalkeeper (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Mike Penders, a 21-year-old goalkeeper who has never made an appearance for Chelsea, was on the bench against Fulham. The Belgian joined last summer from Genk and spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg. Filip Jorgensen, who was the back-up last season, has been sent to Strasbourg on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Both Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville have urged Chelsea to sign a new goalkeeper before the transfer window closes on September 1 to replace Sanchez.

‌



"I do think [there are] concerns defensively," Carragher said on Sky Sports after the Fulham game. "They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Neville added: "I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Sports.title: Gary Neville 'changes mind' on Man Utd as Jamie Carragher drops Premier League predictions
Sports.content:
Gary Neville 'changes mind' on Man Utd as Jamie Carragher drops Premier League predictions

The start of the Premier League campaign has dropped some surprising results which has resulted in some pundits of note performing U-turns

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville wasted no time to start jousting their opinions against each other (Image: YouTube/Sky Sports Premier League)

Jamie Carragher has accused Gary Neville of changing his mind on who will have the better campaign between Manchester United and Liverpool just one match into the new season. United endured the worst possible start when they were beaten 2-0 away to newly-promoted Hull City.

‌



Amid the inquisition of what happened at the MKM Stadium, Andoni Iraola's first Premier League match in charge of the Reds saw them seconds away from defeat. His side trailed Newcastle United 2-1 until Dominik Szoboszlai score a 99th minute penalty to secure a 2-2 draw.

‌



Neville claimed he finds it difficult to guess who will do the best out of Liverpool and United, something Carragher, who believes Arsenal will win the title with Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool following behind them, called him out on during Sky Sports' Monday Night Football.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

When asked to choose between the two Premier League heavyweights, Neville said: " Look, do you want me to be honest? Yes. I can't separate United and Liverpool in fourth place."

Carragher then snapped back: " I've heard you've changed it four times over the weekend. So after United played, he changed it to Liverpool. Liverpool played and he changed it to United."

‌



Neville then replied: " A couple of weeks ago, I had United in third. I didn't have Chelsea where they were, but as you sort of get nearer to the season, you start to look at the squads and you start to think about it.

View 3 Images United were outclassed by Hull City (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"You think about Chelsea and the fact they've got no European football. That'll give them a big edge. I think City are in a better position than United. Look, at the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, really, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

‌



When told to nail down his prediction, Neville crowned Arsenal as his Premier League champions, with Chelsea finishing as runner-up, ahead of City and United. Arsenal, Chelsea and City all began the new campaign with a victory.

Mikel Arteta's side opened their Premier League title difference with a 2-0 dismantling of Coventry City, while the Blues overcame Fulham 3-2 on Monday night. Enzo Maresca's Premier League debut as Manchester City manager also proved dramatic, with late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol securing a 2-1 win over Bournemouth.

View 3 Images Liverpool were seconds away from defeat (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

‌



The aforementioned trio are three of nine teams who began the new Premier League campaign with a victory. Up next in the Premier League, Chelsea host Brighton and Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge.

City play on Friday night when they take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, while Arsenal are not in action until Monday when they face Aston Villa at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Warren thinks Fury-AJ fight will go ahead in America
Sports.content:
Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.

Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".

However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.

Warren told Sky Sports News: "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

"I know there's been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn claimed that Anthony Joshua feels a responsibility to UK fight fans that AJ vs Fury should happen in the UK.

"In the meantime, Tyson [Fury] has flown off to the States, he's in Miami and he's preparing for the fight.

"I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. That's not quite right, actually, they could refuse to fight. We don't get the fight we want to see.

"I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I'm wrong, but I think it will go on in America."

'Nothing unusual' for all-British clash to take place abroad

Warren says the fight taking place outside of the UK would be "nothing unusual" in terms of boxing's history.

"You had two massive American heroes in Muhammad Ali and George Foreman," Warren said. "Two American fighters, all the Americans wanted to see it, Vegas wanted to put the fight on, Madison Square Gardens wanted to see it, and it went off to Zaire.

"Everybody thought: 'What on earth was that all about?' But it became not just an iconic fight and an iconic moment in sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury doesn't hold back as he lashes out at Anthony Joshua as the wait goes on for the pair to confirm a much-anticipated showdown. Credit: @tysonfury.

"Ali had the 'Thrilla in Manila' with Joe Frazier. Joe Bugner fought Ali in Kuala Lumpur, it's nothing unusual.

"I think it's like all sportsmen, say, for example, David Beckham, he went off and played at the end of his career [abroad], and he did that because of the money.

"And that's why these guys are doing this, they are professional boxers.

"Would I like to see it at Wembley? Would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they are in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America."

Sports.title: What is the reality of Villa's finances ahead of Deadline Day?
Sports.content:
All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.

Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Unai Emery was short of words when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins and then after the match said to find out we should call the striker

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

There is mitigation for Villa's bosses, however, who have been frustrated by PSR rules, which they feel have been an ambition killer and stalled their progress.

The switch to Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules this season has only added to that and caused deeper resentment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports explains the new financial Squad Cost Ratio rules that Premier League clubs will have to adhere to this season

As regulars in European competition now, they are limited to spending 70 per cent of their football revenue on transfer fees and player wages.

Remember, they have already been fined twice by UEFA recently, being hit with a £9.5m penalty last year and a £19.4m fine in June, although £13m of that was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement.

That means, inevitably, Villa are a club that has to generate income from player trading in order to buy new talent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher discuss the outgoings of Aston Villa this transfer window and how much of an impact this could have on their season

The proof of that is in the figures from sales over the last three years; Villa have made over £410m selling the likes of Douglas Luiz, Jhon Duran, Jacob Ramsey and Moussa Diaby, before this summer's sale of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

Should Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins follow, that number will be close to the half-a-billion mark, in terms of funds generated.

It is a big ask for Emery to see the castle that he has built taken down keystone by keystone, knowing he has to rebuild again. Last summer, the transfer upheaval contributed to the director of football Monchi leaving the club.

Importantly, Villa currently feel confident their manager is secure. After all, his contract has another three seasons to run, following the bumper new five-year deal he signed in May 2024.

But many of the biggest clubs in Europe have noticed with admiration the job Emery has done at Villa Park, and he will always be on the shortlist of the top clubs for as long as he keeps doing such a stellar job under the circumstances.
