Sports.title: 'Stupid mistakes' - Root 'hacked off' by latest off-field incident
Sports.content:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

Image: Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the day three of the first Test between England and Pakistan as Joe Root's side cruised to an innings victory at Headingley.

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain praise England's winning fast bowler combinations during the three-day victory over Pakistan in first Test.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Sports.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois is determined to fight Baumgardner sooner rather than later

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

Sports.title: Littler and Van Gerwen to headline World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price will headline a packed field competing for a top prize of £100,000 at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals.

The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.

Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael van Gerwen ended his two-year wait for a top-level PDC title by beating Luke Littler at last year's event

Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.

He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

World Matchplay champion Littler enters the tournament as the third seed, while Price, who was beaten by the 19-year-old in the final at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool, is the second seed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler comes into the event after winning the Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January

Luke Humphries also joins the 32-player field as the fourth seed, after he claimed victory at the US Darts masters in June, while New Zealand Darts Masters winner Jonny Clayton and Australian Darts Masters champion James Wade are seeded sixth and seventh, respectively.

Gian van Veen and Stephen Bunting, seeded fifth and eighth, make up the final seeded players on the list.

Those inside the top 24 of the final World Series rankings will gain a berth to play in Amsterdam.

Australian Brody Klinge, who was beaten by Wade in the final of the Australian Darts Masters, will make his debut at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries is also in the field for the World Series of Darts Finals after winning at the US Darts Masters in June

Nathan Aspinall, Josh Rock and Danny Noppert will also join the field, while Ross Smith, who won the Players Championship 20 in June after picking up his maiden European Tour title earlier in the year is also in the field.

Ryan Searle, Wessel Nijman, Chris Dobey and Jermaine Wattimena have also gained tickets to Amsterdam as the four top non-qualified players from the PDC World Rankings as of August 23.

The field was confirmed following Monday night's Tour Card Holder Qualifier in which Rob Cross was among four names to book their place at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Cross bested Dirk van Duijvenbode in Leicester to book his place in Amsterdam, and was joined by Kevin Doets, as well as Karel Sedlacek and Callan Rydz, who will both make their debuts at September's event.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Cross (right) secured his spot at the event folllowing Monday's Tour Card Holder Qualifier

The first round of the tournament will commence over two sessions on Thursday 17 and Friday 18 September, before round two begins on Saturday, September 19.

The finals will then begin on Sunday, September 20, with the quarter-finals set to get under way in the afternoon, before the semi-finals and final later in the evening.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Two goals, some polish and a rebrand: City flip Sávio for quite the profit
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN WINGERS UNDER THE HAMMER

We see Manchester City have managed to flip Savinho for quite the profit. Football Daily had previously assumed this sort of wheeler-dealing was restricted to the Dion-Dublin-adjacent property market, or the Harry-Redknapp-infused used car scene, but it seems we were mistaken. We have no idea how City ended up trousering a £44.2m markup on a player who cost £30.8m two seasons ago, and has achieved the square root of eff all since, but they’ve done it. Consider standing stock still and allowing a ball to clank off you and into the net in an FA Cup tie at Newcastle analogous to installing a new bathroom suite and giving the front room a lick of paint, or taking a microfibre cloth and some polish to the crevices of that grimy dashboard. Result! Goal! Ker-ching! That’s 75 million-nil!

Spurs were the mark, and they could end up paying £85m if all the silverware-related add-ons kick in. So £75m it is, then. But that’s still a fair old whack for an attacking player who scored two goals for City in 53 league appearances. The 22-year-old Brazilian plays on the right flank, so will almost certainly take the place of Mikey Moore, who thought his day at Brentford last weekend had gone badly enough, only for his manager Roberto De Zerbi to go out of his way to namecheck him – and him alone, twice – in his post-match deconstruction of a 3-0 fiasco for which pretty much everyone wearing Tottenham’s traditional blue, gold and dayglo pink was culpable.

Upon signing, Savinho announced that he wishes to be known forthwith as Sávio, reverting to the monicker from his time at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and set up 10 others during a loan stint that was a damn sight more successful than his spell at the Etihad. It’s also his actual name, so there is that. Sávio is far from the first of his countrymen to toy with this most personal of brands – Brazil’s greatest-ever player was actually called Manuel Francisco dos Santos, and Pelé was the result of a name change too – and we’re pretty sure he won’t be the last. Spurs meanwhile will simply be hoping they’re getting the Girona version of their new purchase, because otherwise City will have, in more ways than one, properly flipped them off. Omar Marmoush – 16 goals in 62 appearances, brand-new kitchen worktops, shiny hubcaps – next!

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
