“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York pleads no contest after arrest at Ohio trailer park
Sports.content:
The San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has pleaded no contest to two criminal charges after being arrested at an Ohio trailer park over the weekend.

KRON4 News in San Francisco reported that York was initially arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution but that count was amended to a charge of disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.

A no contest plea is not an admission of guilt but the defendant in question does accept the punishment for the alleged crimes in question. York was sentenced to a day in jail for each count to be served concurrently and was released on Monday morning. He was also fined a total of $1,150 and ordered to complete an online course. The arrest report does not specify what the criminal tools were in York’s case.

According to the New York Post, court documents say York responded to an advert on a website and “arranged to have sexual activity with [a] female in exchange for $140.” York was arrested later arrested at a trailer park in East Palestine, Ohio, on Sunday morning. The East Palestine Police Department and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force were involved in the arrest. York, 46, was born and raised in Youngstown, a 30-minute drive from East Palestine and still has a home in the area.

York is the nephew of former 49ers majority owner Edward J DeBartolo Jr. York took day to day control of the 49ers in 2008 when he became the team’s CEO. After acquiring his mother’s shares, he became the team’s principal owner in 2024.

View image in fullscreen Jed York pictured in a handout from the Colombiana County Sheriff’s Office. Photograph: Colombiana County Sheriff's Office

“As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time,” the 49ers said in a statement. The NFL said in a statement that it is “aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.”

Since York took over as CEO, the 49ers have reached three Super Bowls but lost each time.

He also owns stakes in the Premier League’s Leeds United and Scotland’s Rangers through 49ers Enterprises. He filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May.

Sports.title: Another set of Sullivan brothers are making football waves in Bangladesh
Sports.content:
Ronan Sullivan had tried a panenka twice in his life. Both attempts were at practice on the other side of the world, and one hit the crossbar. But his twin brother, Declan, was hardly surprised when Ronan turned to him and told him he’d chip the fifth penalty of a shootout that could win a scoreless tournament final, as millions tuned in online to see his Bangladesh side play against India in the Under-20 South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championship.

“He didn’t even need to say it. I knew he was gonna do that the whole time,” Declan remembered, sitting next to his brother on the couch of their dorm room at Saint Joseph’s University. “I knew that if he got the last pen to win it, he was gonna do that. That’s just the him thing to do.”

Moments later the ball gracefully splashed into the back of the net, and the thousands in attendance on 3 April in Malé, Maldives erupted.

“I wouldn’t have believed you if you told me it [would have] went like that,” Ronan said.

Less than two years after he began exchanging messages on Instagram with the “Save Bangladesh Football” fan page, the brothers were celebrating a U-20 title, made possible by their maternal ancestry, as members of essentially the home team. (Bangladesh is the largest source of migrant workers in the Maldives.)

“Flying in there alone was incredible. Like the water’s so blue. I’ve never seen anything like it. Like we go to Ocean City, New Jersey, where the water is brown, and it’s our favorite place ever,” Ronan said. “So when we saw this water, we were like, ‘Oh my gosh!’ It looked like the water from [the movie] The Waterboy. At the end [of the movie], that special water … I think it’s just Maldives water.”

The story seems ripped from the pages of a Hollywood script. Two kids from Philadelphia with very Irish names who had never visited Bangladesh before their tryout for the country’s U-20 squad prior to the tournament, then returned to its crowded capital triumphantly. They allowed a few days for the media frenzy, and a few more for themselves to explore, enjoy the food and time with their grandmother, whom they’d only seen in the US until this trip.

But this could be part of the opening scene for Bangladesh, ranked 181st by Fifa, with nearly 180 million people and, according to the United Nations, the world’s sixth-largest diaspora. The vast majority of it is concentrated in southern Asia or the Middle East, but there’s a well-established community in the UK, growing ones in the US and Italy, and pockets elsewhere in the West.

“I think a lot of people saw what we did over there and saw how good of an experience that was, and now all of a sudden I’m seeing a lot of foreign players interested in playing for Bangladesh, a couple kids from England who are on pretty good academies over there, so we have talent all around the world. It’s just about utilizing that,” Declan said.

The Sullivans are well known in Bangladesh, the US and beyond, and so too is former US men’s national team captain Thomas Dooley. The son of an American serviceman who grew up and played in Germany then joined the USMNT by happenstance, Dooley was announced as the head coach of the Bangladesh senior team seven weeks after the U-20 side brought a trophy home. He spent most of the coaching chapter of his life in Southeast Asia, where he heard about “a fanatic country in football” he is now leading into a new World Cup cycle.

“We are a country of being fans. We need to change that. We need to be a country of playing football,” Dooley told the Guardian. “That’s what we need to be, and we need to find a way to do that.”

View image in fullscreen The Bangladesh U-20 national team celebrate winning the SAFF Championship. Photograph: Courtesy Bangladesh Football Federation

Ronan, Declan, and their brothers Quinn and Cavan – both attackers for the Philadelphia Union – were eligible to play for the US and Germany as well as Bangladesh. While Quinn was cap-tied by the USMNT last summer and Manchester-City bound Cavan is a top American prospect, the twins were more realistic bets for Bangladesh.

“It all started with an Instagram DM, which is kind of crazy,” Declan recalled. The message came from that Save Bangladesh Football account. Initially confused that a fan page was encouraging them to come for a camp before they had a passport, Ronan and Declan soon realized the account was a legitimate asset and facilitator for the federation, eventually connecting the Sullivans to federation vice-president Fahad Karim when they expressed interest in the SAFF U-20 tournament.

“[We had] a bit of time before college. It would be awesome to go play, represent the country, become more part of the culture,” Ronan said. The next three months were “a bit of a crazy process,” primarily because obtaining a Bangladeshi passport when their mother didn’t have one wasn’t straightforward. But in March the twins flew from New York to Delhi, then Delhi to Dhaka, easily the longest journey of their lives.

There wasn’t a red carpet waiting for them, though. They had not been promised spots in the squad, arriving for a camp with more than 30 players, including three fellow “origin” players whom the Sullivans knew of and could easily communicate with. The manager spoke English too but on the pitch, to varying degrees, there was a language barrier.

“When you’re foreign, it’s harder to get the ball at first because you don’t speak the language and maybe the guys weren’t super thrilled that we’re there. But once you get the ball a couple times and show what you can do, it helps out,” Ronan said. After a few days of training they were confident they’d make the roster, and socially their integration progressed.

Dooley adamantly defends the right of players with Bangladeshi roots to choose their national team. His Asian coaching odyssey started in the Philippines, where he shrugged off many fans resistant to foreign-born recruits, and he’s encouraged by the culture of the Bangladesh senior team he’s inherited, highlighting the leadership and humility of Leicester City midfielder Hamza Choudhury.

“Everybody was happy that Hamza came in, and they understand – the players understand that international players can help them because they can look up to them,” Dooley said. “What kind of attitude they have, the work ethic that they bring in. So everything, they can look up to them, how they handle stuff.”

The more they search for players abroad, the more they find – not necessarily in a major European league but at a level that can raise the standard of the pool. But it’s a balancing act. Dooley is getting “thousands” of messages about players and acknowledges “we have to be careful,” noting the budgetary constraints.

“It’s not everybody who sends a picture of a free kick that he does is a good player, or maybe can help us. We have good players in this country over here too that we can actually afford,” he said. “We are not spending $2,000, $3,000 on a player to bring him over, and he’s sitting on the bench. So if the players who are coming over are the ones that really can help us, otherwise we’re using that money and putting all the local players in the camp and train them twice a day for two weeks, and you will see that they’re getting much, much better.”

Dooley says that coaching a decent group of players who can cover plenty of ground to change the way they think about the game – “most of the players, they don’t think, they play” – and to limit mistakes can improve the team 20 to 30%. He thinks climbing to the 150s of the FIFA rankings is certainly achievable.

Of course, there’s a much bigger dream than that.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celebrations at the SAFF U-20 Championship in the Maldives. Photograph: Save Bangladesh Football/Courtesy Save Bangladesh Football

The Instagram comment sections of all four Sullivan brothers have been flooded with Bangladeshi flags for years. The twins were checking their phones in the Maldives, absorbing as the buzz online reached a different stratosphere. They noticed the rivalry with India in particular.

“They were making edits of me walking a dog that was painted like the Indian flag. Like it was crazy. There was a lot of heat there, for sure. A lot of tension,” Ronan said.

The fervent support in the Maldives created an atmosphere they had never felt on the pitch, a surreal experience that carried into a heroes’ welcome in Dhaka.

“That was a lot. Got a lot of flowers, met a lot of people. I feel like our team was the hot new thing in Bangladesh,” Declan said. Indeed, when the Sullivan twins walked around Dhaka they already stood out because, in Declan’s words, “we’re white, for everyone there at least.”

“We met a bunch of people, and everyone was so happy and so grateful that we brought the trophy back to the country. Like they were really, really hype about that, and that’s not something you would see in America [for] youth soccer.”

And you probably wouldn’t see a media presence at the airport for a senior national team almost anywhere, no matter the circumstances, comparable to what met Dooley at the airport when his group departed for a friendly against San Marino in June.

“I thought we are going to the World Cup,” Dooley said. “I was like, this is amazing, and I cannot imagine [the scene] if we would qualify for the World Cup.”

“I think the country would explode if we qualify for a World Cup,” Ronan said.

It seems far-fetched. No country from the Indian subcontinent has ever appeared at a men’s or women’s World Cup. Its viral passion for international soccer continues to be channeled towards South American giants.

However, with further expansion of the men’s World Cup looking inevitable, and a bridge to their diaspora being built, a new dimension awaits this sport in Bangladesh. Something even greater awaits if a country from the subcontinent can qualify. While recruiting players is increasingly common in international sport, what it could unlock in this scenario is rare.

“Whenever I think about the 64 team [World Cup], I’m thinking, ‘Look, if we get all these players, we have a chance to qualify.’ Like, that’s the dream. That’s the ultimate goal,” Declan said. He mentioned his friend, former Union academy teammate and Penn State winger Nehan Hasan, and Stanford striker Trevor Islam as possible additions, and hopes there will be many more candidates.

“We have to convince them. We have to tell them you can actually leave a legacy here in this country,” Dooley said about eligible players.

Dooley preaches qualifying for the Asian Cup (the Bangladesh men only have once in their history) or the World Cup is a process, but in the same breath he says “it can go fast”. He mentions 19-year-old winger and Fulham academy product Farhaan Wahid and 25-year-old Louie Watson, an attacking midfielder in the English fourth division, as the next potential pieces for his project. Choudhury and a New York Cosmos summer signing, Canada-born midfielder Shamit Shome, are the cornerstones. Dooley stresses that goalkeeper will be a key position to address.

After their fall friendlies, the next notable step for the program will be the senior level SAFF Championship in Bangladesh in November. Bangladesh have won the tournament just once, as hosts in 2003. It’s Dooley’s main focus, but after that, he’s planning to be more involved in the development of the sport domestically. In his view, it’s a top-down mission: the success of the senior team drives the interest, sponsorship, and investment for a proper pyramid structure, with youth academies feeding adult leagues.

Until he moves into an apartment in the affluent Gulshan area of Dhaka, Dooley is living at a hotel. He’ll look out the window at densely populated high-rise buildings, lamenting only a school or two in sight with a soccer field. This is the deeper challenge, one of infrastructure, culture and mindset for the next generation.

“We would love to have the kids not want to be a fan of Argentina. They want to be a player to play against Argentina, against Brazil,” he said.

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge.

They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.

It could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.

At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.

Perhaps what’s most striking, though, is how different the approach is to Enzo Maresca’s. Where Maresca prioritised control to often stultifying effect, Alonso’s game is based on rapid turnovers and transition. It’ll probably settle down as his systems become deeper rooted but there was a sense of recklessness at times to their play. It was harum-scarum, end-to-end, thrilling stuff, which is all very well to watch, and may even come as a relief after the sterility of Maresca and the shambles of Liam Rosenior, but may not be great for consistency or sustained runs of form.

Alonso could hardly have dreamed of a quicker start, João Pedro putting Chelsea ahead after 31 seconds, matching the record for the quickest goal scored in the reign of a Premier League manager, David Unsworth’s goal – also against Fulham – in David Moyes’s first game in charge of Everton in March 2002. João Pedro had scored eight goals in eight pre-season games; and this a player Maresca told not to focus on scoring goals shortly before he went on a run of seven games without a shot. That was a first indication of a forward line starting to show signs of an impressive understanding. All three combined for the third goal, Morgan Rogers flicking on for João Pedro who held the ball up for the overlapping Palmer to slip his shot cleverly between Bernd Leno’s legs.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro (second from left), Cole Palmer (second from right) and Morgan Rogers (right) combined impressively on their first outing as Chelsea’s front three. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Alonso’s first go at finding a pattern amid the legions of players assembled by BlueCo involved a midfield made up of two players who, despite being at Chelsea together for the past three years, had never previously been paired in the centre: Roméo Lavia and Reece James. It was not entirely by choice: Moisés Caicedo was left out as a precaution while Enzo Fernández remained on the bench until the 65th minute as Manchester City continue their pursuit of him. And it didn’t entirely work. It may look a defensively robust pairing but there were long spells when Fulham had control of midfield.

A feature of Alonso’s approach, and one of the reasons it takes time and commitment to learn – qualities that were notably lacking at Real Madrid – is that players can emerge in unexpected positions. Which doesn’t entirely explain how the right-sided centre-back Maxence Lacroix found himself running on to Palmer’s pass in the Fulham box but, having got there, he demonstrated great poise to skip around Jorge Cuenca and cut the ball back for Rogers to score his first Chelsea goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet for all that was new and positive, and for all that was raw and unintentionally exciting, there was one glaring and inexplicably familiar failing for Chelsea: in goal. Sánchez’s positioning seemed very strange for Fulham’s first goal, drilled in at his near post by Josh King (who also benefited from a bizarrely ineffectual attempt to track from Rogers), and while it was a far less glaring error, he pushed Timothy Castagne’s shot straight to Gonzalo García for Fulham’s second.

Although Sánchez doesn’t perhaps quite deserve the negative reputation he has among certain Chelsea fans, he did make a league-high five errors leading to goals in 2024-25 and three last season. It remains mystifying that a club that signs wide forwards by the dozen continues to refuse to invest in a top-class goalkeeper. That may yet hold Chelsea back.

Generally, though, Alonso can be satisfied with his start: a win against Chelsea’s local rivals, an impressive display from Acheampong, a number of fluent interactions from his front three and plenty of signs of his system beginning to take hold, with a few obvious improvements to be made. And from the point of view of fans and casual observers, it looks like it should be fun.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

A first FA Cup final was a historic moment for Brighton. Despite losing to Manchester City at Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.

It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.

Brighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.

The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victory over City and a draw against Arsenal and will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s side at Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.

Off-field picture

Pinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction of Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.

The manager

Now entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style. He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.

Star signing

The acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.

View image in fullscreen Lia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton. Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Brighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.

Set for a breakthrough

Sophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.

What they say …

“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.” – Lia Wälti

Where are they playing their home games?

Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.

Sports.title: ‘He’s the best’ – Jose Mourinho exposes subtle detail in journalist’s question
Sports.content:
Spanish journalists will have to do a lot better if they want to catch Jose Mourinho slipping.

At a press conference ahead of Real Madrid's LaLiga clash against Real Sociedad, one reporter remarked people inside the club told him Mourinho appeared 'much more relaxed and calm.'



2 Mourinho is already enjoying the limelight in the Spanish capital Credit: Getty

Although it may have been intended as a compliment, there was a curious detail in the reporter's comment that Mourinho latched on to.

What did Jose Mourinho say to the journalist?

"So you have a source inside the club? Good to know," Mourinho replied.

The reporter later noted to Mourinho he had 'a lot' of contacts within the walls of the Bernabeu, prompting another intriguing retort from the Portuguese icon.



"A lot?" Mourinho said.

"You say good things, but if you speak bad of me, be careful."

Mourinho's press conference antics had a number of Madridistas in awe, with one remarking on X: "He's the best."

Jose Mourinho enjoys winning return at Real Madrid

Perhaps the 63-year-old is indeed a more relaxed figure after his second stint in charge of the Spanish giants got off to a dream start.



Summer signing Carlos Espi struck in the 90th minute to help Real secure a 2-1 win over Espanyol.

Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in the ninth minute before Espanyol's Alex Calatrava responded on the half-hour mark.



But Espi ensured there would be one final twist shortly before full time.

2 Espi, who joined Real for £21m this summer, has already won a space in Mourinho's heart Credit: AFP

Kylian Mbappe drove into the box but had the ball poked away from him. Fortunately for Espi, he was in the right place at the right time as he collected the ball and nudged it out of his feet before firing into the net from close range.

When is Real Madrid next game?

Real will aim to make it two wins from two to start the domestic campaign on Wednesday against Real Sociedad at the Bernabeu.



The San Sebastian-based club opened their LaLiga account with a 1-0 loss away to Real Betis.

Real and Mourinho will then cast their attention towards Thursday's Champions League draw, which will be held at UEFA's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

The draw begins at 5pm BST.

Sports.title: Randal Kolo Muani dug out by new manager just weeks after £32million transfer
Sports.content:
Randal Kolo Muani dug out by new manager just weeks after £32million transfer

Randal Kolo Muani has been openly criticised by Juventus manager Luciano Spalletti after just one game of the new season.

Spalletti called out Kolo Muani for thinking he is playing at 'an exceptional level' when the boss believes that isn't the case.



3 Kolo Muani has faced some tough comments from his boss one game into the season Credit: Getty

The French striker, who spent last season on loan at Tottenham, had three shots in Juve's 1-0 win over Frosinone on Sunday.

But he missed one big chance and only hit the target once, also committing two fouls and completing 58 per cent of his passes.

And his performance hasn't pleased Spalletti, who wasted no time in digging out his new forward.



The Italian also suggested another striker would come in this summer to provide competition for Kolo Muani.

What did Spalletti say about Kolo Muani?

"We went out and got him, we nurtured him, and we know his true worth," Spalletti said on Kolo Muani to DAZN.



"But he needs to realise that he hasn't played for two years - and there's a reason for that.

"Sometimes you think you're at an exceptional level, but in reality, you've left something behind and need to go back and reclaim it."



The Juve manager added: "He knows how to hold up the ball and find space, and he is physically strong...

"But these are matches where he needs to deliver goals. The spaces were all there for him to exploit."

"We are also looking for someone with different characteristics," Spalletti went on to reveal, hinting at another striker coming in to potentially challenge Kolo Muani for a starting spot.

3 Spalletti is clearly not happy with what he is seeing from Kolo Muani at Juve Credit: Getty



3 The Frenchman only scored one Premier League goal for Spurs last season Credit: Getty

Kolo Muani's recent struggles

Kolo Muani joined the Italian giants earlier this month, signing for the club from Paris Saint-Germain for £32.4million.

Spalletti clearly thinks Kolo Muani has to up his game if he wants to succeed at Juventus following a rough couple of years.

He had not played a game for PSG since December 2024 before his permanent exit from France this summer.



A loan spell at Juve in the first half of 2025 bought him some success though, as he scored eight goals in 16 Serie A appearances.

However, after joining Tottenham on loan last year, his goals dried up, with Kolo Muani scoring just five times in 41 games.

Only one of his goals came in the Premier League as he struggled to make an impact for relegation-threatened Spurs.

Now, Juve have signed him for a second time, hoping that he can recapture his form from his previous stint.



But it seems he's not made the most impressive start, with Spalletti desperate to see some more from the 27-year-old.

Sports.title: ‘Difficult to put into words’ – EFL player retires at 28 after suffering fractured skull and bleed on brain
Sports.content:
‘Difficult to put into words’ – EFL player retires at 28 after suffering fractured skull and bleed on brain

Fleetwood Town defender Denver Hume has retired with immediate effect after a 10-month injury lay-off.

The left-back has not played since October last year after suffering a fractured skull in training.



3 Hume has retired aged 28 after suffering a fractured skull and brain bleed in training Credit: Getty

Hume was left with a bleed on his brain after a collision during a session.

He has now been advised to hang up his boots just two weeks after turning 28.

Hume announces retirement

The Sunderland academy graduate confirmed his decision to retire in an emotional statement shared to social media.



Writing on Instagram, he admitted: "I never thought I’d be writing this at the age of 28, but following specialist medical advice, my career as a professional footballer has come to an end.

"After suffering a fractured skull and bleed on the brain last season, I’ve spent the months since trying to process this and find a way back to doing what I love the most.



"Unfortunately that isn’t going to be possible and is something I’ve had to come to terms with."

Hume made 188 senior club appearances across spells with Sunderland, Portsmouth, Grimsby Town and Fleetwood.



His career saw him feature in the Championship, League One and League Two.

He added: "To every coach, staff member, teammate and supporter who’s been part of my journey - thank you.

"And most importantly, to my family, girlfriend and those closest to me. Thank you for every sacrifice, piece of advice, and being there through the highest and lowest moments. I couldn’t have done any of this without you.

3 The left-back has not played since suffering the injury in October 2025 Credit: Getty



"Football has been a huge part of who I am and all I’ve known, but I’m excited to discover what life looks like beyond being a footballer.

"I’m incredibly grateful and proud of the journey I’ve had in the game, and I’m looking forward to seeing what the next chapter brings."

Hume's EFL career

Hume began his career with Sunderland, where he won the EFL Trophy in 2021.

He later moved to Portsmouth in January 2022, where he spent two years.



A 17-month stint with Grimsby followed after his arrival in early 2024.

During his time at Blundell Park, Hume was named in both the EFL and PFA Team of the Year for the 2024/25 season.

3 Hume had spells with Sunderland, Portsmouth, Grimsby and Fleetwood during his career Credit: Getty

His performances for the Mariners earned a move to Fleetwood last summer.



However, Hume made just nine appearances before suffering his now career-ending injury in training last October.

Sports.title: Rafael Leao in talks over Premier League move in final week of transfer window
Sports.content:
Rafael Leao in talks over Premier League move in final week of transfer window

Aston Villa have held talks with AC Milan over signing Rafael Leao, talkSPORT understands.

The Portugal winger has previously expressed his desire to explore a 'new challenge' this summer, insisting he would be open to a move to the Premier League.

4 Rafael Leao joined Milan in a £30million deal in 2019 Credit: AFP

And Leao could now be offered his opportunity in English football, with Villa keen to bolster their forward line.

Unai Emery's side look set to lose striker Ollie Watkins, as talkSPORT understands Al Hilal are confident they will be able to complete a deal for the striker before the transfer window closes.

The Saudi Pro League have seen four bids for the England international rejected, who has now returned to Villa training.

Watkins was not included in the matchday squad for his side's Premier League opener against Brighton - which ended in a 4-0 defeat - having expressed his desire to leave and join Al Hilal.

Leao in, Watkins out?

With Watkins looking increasingly likely to depart, Villa have turned their attention to attacking reinforcements.

And Leao appears to be among their targets, with talks taking place between Milan and the Villans over a potential move.

The 26-year-old is contracted with the Italian giants until 2028, but club chiefs have been reluctant to offer him a new deal, with the player and club having an often fractious relationship.

Leao can play as a centre forward or on the left wing and scored nine goals and added three assists in 29 Serie A appearances last season.

The Portuguese could be seen as a direct replacement for Morgan Rogers, who left to join Chelsea in a £117million deal.

He would also battle Alejandro Garnacho for a starting spot under Emery.

4 Al Hilal remain confident they will sign Watkins despite his return to Villa training Credit: Getty

4 Mateta could be set to depart Crystal Palace after four years at Selhurst Park Credit: Getty

Leao isn't Villa's only attacking target, with Crystal Palace rejecting an opening bid to sign centre-forward Jean-Philippe Mateta.

The Frenchman is seen as an alternative to Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson, who has long been a target of the West Midlands outfit.

Emery's side are frontrunners to sign Jackson, with talkSPORT recently revealing the Blues are set to demand £65m for the Senegal international.

Beyond forward line reinforcements, talkSPORT also understands Villa are also in advanced talks over a move for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez.

Villa are trying to agree a loan with an obligation to buy for the Ecuadorian centre back.

This comes after having two offers rejected by Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis, and south coast sources have told talkSPORT the two clubs remain some way apart in their valuations.

4 Leao has made nearly 300 appearances for Milan since joining from Lille in 2019 Credit: Getty

What has Leao said about his future?

Earlier this summer, Leao announced publicly he wants a new challenge after seven years with Milan, having long been linked with a move to the Premier League - with Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United all previously credited with interest

In June, he told SportTV: “I want a new challenge out of Serie A.

“I already won two trophies in Italy and have been there for a while. The league is evolving, but for my style of football, I think the Premier League or LaLiga would make more of my talent, as a player.

“If a Premier League opportunity were to come along, I would be very happy.

"I think that I can put my talent up against the players there, who are of a very high level. Playing in that kind of a league really gets the best out of a player.

“Let’s see what will happen this summer.”

Sports.title: FA Cup winner reveals sympathetic linesman saved him on EFL debut in front of Arsenal scout
Sports.content:
FA Cup winner reveals sympathetic linesman saved him on EFL debut in front of Arsenal scout

Jeff Stelling had the chance to sit down with someone who can also consider Hartlepool United as having a major impact on their career.

Former Arsenal defender Carl Jenkinson made his Football League debut against the talkSPORT Breakfast host's beloved Monkey Hangers and found himself instantly indebted to the linesman.



3 Jenkinson was fortunate to have avoided a red card on his Football League debut against Hartlepool Credit: PA

The 34-year-old announced his retirement earlier this month, having been released by Bromley at the end of last season.

It brought the curtain down on a 16-year playing career that started when he came through the youth ranks at Charlton.

The Addicks academy graduate was handed his Football League debut in February 2011 against Hartlepool in League One.



Just seven minutes into the second half, Jenkinson replaced the injured Simon Francis in a 2-1 defeat at Victoria Park.

Hartlepool superfan Stelling delighted in reminding the one-cap England international of the result on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"It was at Hartlepool," Stelling reminisced. "February 2011. It must have been blooming freezing. And I'm delighted to say we won 2-1.

"Couldn't let you go without reminding you!"

Jenkinson replied: "That was the one, where I spoke about: I flew into a tackle straight after I came onto the pitch and I was lucky to walk away with a yellow.



"And it was the linesman who said to me in my ear, 'Don't worry, I'll tell the ref it was just the yellow.'

"I ended up getting a run in the team after that. Whereas, I could have obviously got a red."

3 Jenkinson later joked in interviews that he 'would love to buy that linesman a beer' Credit: PA:Empics Sport

Jenkinson previously revealed to A-Leagues All Access that an Arsenal scout was in attendance to watch his debut.



What may have happened to the defender had he been sent off that day is anybody's guess, but instead he went on to make seven consecutive league starts for Charlton following his debut.

Jenkinson went on to sign for Arsenal that summer, where he went on to lift the FA Cup with now-Gunners manager Mikel Arteta in 2014.

His one senior cap for England came two years earlier when he featured for Roy Hodgson's Three Lions against Sweden in 2012.

He ultimately made 70 appearances for Arsenal, with his one and only goal for the club coming in a 2-0 win at Norwich on the final day of the 2013/14 Premier League campaign.



Jenkinson has been a talkSPORT regular since leaving Arsenal, having previously revealed the best Gunners team he ever played with, while also likening ex-teammate Arteta to club legend Thierry Henry.

3 Jenkinson appeared as a studio guest for Arsenal's 3-0 opening-day win over Coventry City Credit: Getty

What is Carl Jenkinson doing now?

Jenkinson returned to England with Bromley two years ago following a stint in the A-League with Melbourne City in Australia.

Injuries restricted him to just five League Two outings last season as Bromley won the title to secure their place in England's third tier.



Reflecting on having now retired, Jenkinson told talkSPORT: "Enjoying my weekends. Just a bit of time with my fiancée doing different things.

"We just went to Brighton at the weekend, which you can never do when you've got a game of footy.

"So, yeah, just keeping busy, doing different stuff in the gym a lot, because I love that side of stuff; A bit of media work here and there."

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott given perfect Premier League club to join before Deadline Day
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott given perfect Premier League club to join before Deadline Day

Harvey Elliott has been told he cannot afford a repeat of his 2025/26 campaign this season.

The Liverpool midfielder endured a torrid loan spell at Aston Villa, who were unwilling to make his move permanent.

3 Elliott has been told he cannot afford another season without regular first-team action Credit: Getty

Villa's deal to sign Elliott included an obligation to buy for £35million if he made 10 Premier League appearances.

With his loan club deciding against meeting the clause, the 23-year-old was limited to just four league appearances for the club.

Having returned to Anfield this summer, Elliott featured heavily in pre-season under new manager Andoni Iraola.

However, he was left out of the matchday squad for Sunday's draw at Newcastle United.

Elliott's next club?

Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist have now tipped the former England Under-21 international for a move to St. James' Park.

The pair discussed Elliott's future on Tuesday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.

Referencing his snub from the squad, Stelling explained: "He must have been devastated at the weekend.

"His contract is up next summer, so this is not going to cost the king’s ransom. What are we talking, £15-20million? Something like that.

"I was going to look at the newly-promoted sides like Coventry, but would he be out of place at Newcastle, somewhere like that?"

McCoist agreed, replying: "No, I don't think he would."

3 Elliott made just nine appearances on loan at Villa from Liverpool last season Credit: Getty

The ex-Scotland striker added: "He wouldn’t look out of place in that Newcastle side and Newcastle are looking for players who are (similar to) the players they’ve lost. Obviously, Anthony Gordon would spring to mind.

"The most important thing, and it’s massively important for Harvey Elliott this season, last season was a write-off, he can’t afford another one like that."

Iraola's stance on Elliott

Iraola had previously revealed Elliott would have a chance to earn a place in the squad during the summer.

The new Reds boss had been asked about his future during his introductory press conference last month.

Speaking to reporters, Iraola explained: "I've seen him with this eagerness to show himself.

"He will have a chance during the pre-season. He came one week earlier and I hope we can see him in a good place.

3 Elliott was left out of the squad for Liverpool's season opener despite featuring heavily in pre-season Credit: Getty

"Last season had to have been very difficult for him as it was a strange situation that meant they [Aston Villa] couldn't let him play."

Elliott was part of Liverpool's pre-season tour of the USA, featuring in matches against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds United.

The playmaker even provided an assist in a 4-2 win over the Black Cats.

He later appeared in further friendlies against both Monaco and Como ahead of the new season.

Sports.title: Ashley Cole quits England coaching role after five years as Lee Carsley pays tribute
Sports.content:
Ashley Cole quits England coaching role after five years as Lee Carsley pays tribute

Ashley Cole has stepped away from his coaching role with the England Under-21s.

The former England star joined the Young Lions set-up in 2021.

2 Cole has been an influential figure in England's youth system Credit: Getty

He was part of the coaching team that won back-to-back European Under-21s Championships in 2023 and 2025.

Cole also served as assistant to Under-21s boss Lee Carsley when he took charge of the senior team on an interim basis.

The ex-Arsenal and Chelsea left-back also served in a broader role with the FA, supporting development pathways into the men's team.

Carsley said: "I want to pay tribute to Ashley who played a major part in our two Euro wins and also had a key role in the current campaign with his tactical and technical knowledge.

"As well as being an important part of our coaching team, he also had a positive, inspirational impact on the players given his own elite experience.

"I am certain he will have even more success in his coaching career whatever the future holds."

Cole's coaching career

The iconic Premier League left-back has been a trusted assistant to both Frank Lampard and Wayne Rooney in recent years.

Cole has held roles working under his former England teammates at Derby and Birmingham in the Championship, as well as Chelsea and Everton in the Premier League.

His first head coach role came earlier this year when he took charge of Serie B side Cescena in Italy.

The 45-year-old was appointed in March on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

2 Carsley formed a fruitful coaching partnership with Cole for the Young Lions Credit: Getty

Cole stepped down after winning just one match out of his eight in charge.

Next steps

The Champions League and Premier League winner is trying to establish himself as a head coach after years of experience in various assistant roles.

Speaking earlier this year, Cole admitted he grew frustrated with the lack of opportunities in English football.

"I was getting kind of discouraged by a lack of opportunities, from some clubs in England I spoke to," Cole said.

“They like to throw the 'you don't have experience' line. And I'm like, I get what you're saying, I agree - but how am I going to get experience?

"That's the battle you have to fight as a number two for six or seven years - you have to take a leap of faith, but a club also has to take a leap of faith.

"I don't think there are too many black English coaches working in Italy, so yes, it is a massive leap of faith from them and I'm very proud to be here.

"It is a great place to be and to start. I'm glad I'm back. We're going to do something different - a bit special."

Sports.title: EFL stadium forced to shut and postpone match due to annual music festival
Sports.content:
EFL stadium forced to shut and postpone match due to annual music festival

Portsmouth Women's home fixture with AFC Wimbledon has been postponed due to a clash with a local music festival.

Pompey had been due to host the Dons at Fratton Park on Sunday in their third league game of the season.

2 Fratton Park will be hosting all of Portsmouth Women's home games in the 2026/27 campaign Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

But the clash will now be taking place at a later date, after it was postponed to accommodate the annual Victorious Festival.

The music festival is set to welcome around 80,000 ticketholders per day, with the event running between Friday and Sunday.

It is taking place on Portsmouth's Southsea Common and Castle Field, located just over two miles from Fratton Park.

With over 200,000 people expected over three days, the festival will welcome some huge names - namely The Verve frontman Richard Ashcroft, as well as chart-topping bands Bastille and Kasabian.

As a result, huge disruption is anticipated across the city, prompting Portsmouth to move their upcoming clash with Wimbledon.

Portsmouth statement

Announcing the fixture change on social media, a Pompey statement read: “This Sunday’s fixture between Pompey Women and AFC Wimbledon at Fratton Park has been postponed due to a clash with Victorious Festival.

"A new date for the rearranged fixture will be announced shortly."

Confirming the news to their supporters, Wimbledon wrote: "MATCH POSTPONED.

“This Sunday’s fixture between Portsmouth and AFC Wimbledon at Fratton Park has been postponed due to a clash with this weekend’s Victorious Festival, which causes major disruption to the whole city.

“A new date for the fixture will be announced shortly.”

With the rescheduled fixture date yet to be confirmed, both sides will be hoping to boost their points tallies in the meantime.

The Victorious Festival won't affect Portsmouth men's weekend fixtures, who are away to Bristol City on Saturday.

John Mousinho's side are looking to make it back-to-back wins at Ashton Gate after winning their last match against Lincoln City, as they look to outperform talkSPORT's prediction of a 17th-place Championship finish this term.

Portsmouth and AFC Wimbledon's women's sides compete in the Women's National League Southern Premier Division - the third tier of women's football.

Portsmouth are level on points with Wimbledon after their opening two league games, with both sides boasting three points.

The Dons sit a place higher than Pompey on goal difference, currently occupying fourth place.

2 The upcoming Victorious Festival is expected to bring more than 200,000 people to Portsmouth this weekend Credit: Getty

They have made almost identical starts to the campaign, with both sides losing their openers to Bournemouth and Portsmouth respectively.

But both sides then got their first wins of the campaign in their second games, with Portsmouth thumping Swindon 4-0.

Meanwhile Wimbledon thrashed Plymouth 6-0 to give their goal difference a considerable boost.

The Dons will next be in league action on Sunday, September 13, welcoming Real Bedford to Imperial Fields, while Pompey travel to Hill Park to take on Saltdean United.

Sports.title: Wrexham set to land Man City defender Kabore, Savinho welcomes 'brilliant opportunity' after completing £85m Spurs move... and Aston Villa explore finances for Rafael Leao deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League. Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020. Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested. Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham Bees still buzzing about Diouf Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season. West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre. The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league. AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him . Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City. They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah. Wrexham close on £8m move Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push. Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million. Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers. Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old. Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m. They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti. NATHAN SALT Olympiacos in for Edson Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan. The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far. Doncaster living the life O'Reilly Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan. A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe. Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season Tottenham seal Savinho deal Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho. Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons. Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City. Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world. 'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.' De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity. 'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.' Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs Pinnock in for Coventry medical Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend. The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday. Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor. Villa look at Leao deal Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao. Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well. Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea Bakwa off to Lille Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan. The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact. He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille. Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground City set to go back to Enzo Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez. The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet. But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.
